“Reversion to lower stage in a time scale by reducing two increments” was imposed. Again during 2022, he has put-in 
only 2-musters. Charge sheet dt.l8.0.2023 was issued, he submitted explanation on 0.08.2023 and enquiry was 
conducted on 0I.09.2023 and show cause notice was issued. But, the petitioner failed to submit any explanation to the 
show cause notice and as the charges were proved against the petitioner, the respondents’ company was constrained to 
dismiss the petitioner from service vide Ref. dt.29.08.2025. 


3(c). The Respondent Company is providing Medical facilities (as in and out patients) to its employees and their 
dependants through its Hospitals and if required the patients will be referred to higher centers for further 
treatment/diagnosis. In the same manner, the petitioner was also extended medical facilities by this Respondent 
Company for the ailments which he was suffering for. The petitioner has not reported sick in Company’s Hospitals 
during the entire absenteeism period till September, 2023. The petitioner being a habitual and chronic absentee, the 
Respondents’ Company was constrained to dismiss the Petitioner due to his misconduct. The petitioner was not kept 
in sick list and was examined by the main hospital and found fit for duty. The averments made by the petitioner in his 
petition are false and baseless. He was given full and fair opportunity and natural justice principles were followed 
during the enquiry proceedings. He accepted the charges leveled against him and pleaded guilty during enquiry 
proceedings. He did not submit any documentary evidence and not produced any witness and the charges were 
proved. 


3(d). Further, the Petitioner admitted in the enquiry Proceedings that he has not reported sick in any company’s 
Hospital during the absenteeism Period. The averments made at para 7 of the annexure to the Petition that the 
respondent No.2 unjustly dismissed him from Service vide ref 29.08.2025 straight away without issuing any prior 
show cause Notice are totally false hence denied. The dismissal of the petitioner was not done "straight away" or 
without a show cause notice proposing dismissal. The letters dt.!9/25.03.202l, 0/I.02.2022, 25.07.2022 explicitly 
gave many opportunities to the petitioner. The petitioner's failure to attend (346) days of work during 2022 proved his 
unwillingness to improve, leaving dismissal as the only course of action. He was given number of opportunities to 
correct himself and to be regular to his duties by imposing minor penalties such as stoppage of one increment without 
cumulative effect during 209, Reversion to lower stage in a time scale by reducing two (02) increments 2020 and 
202. But, he failed to improve his attendance and resorted to unauthorizedly absent for duty during the calendar years 
2022, and as there was no change in his attendance, the Respondent Company was constrained to dismiss the 
Petitioner. The dismissal of petitioner/Gunti Sadanandam was justified and final disciplinary action following a long 


[भाग —avs 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 553 


history of habitual and unauthorized absenteeism. The management provided multiple opportunities to the petitioner 
to improve, including counseling with the employee, warnings, suspensions, stoppage of increments and reversion to 
lower grade by reducing (02) increments. Despite being found fit for duty by the company's medical staff, he failed to 
attend work during this final review period, demonstrating a complete lack of interest in his job. 


3(e). The company has adhered to all procedural norms, including conducting a fair inquiry and processing his 
terminal benefits, such as his CMPF and gratuity payments. As the petitioner did not improve his attendance in spite 
of giving many opportunities, the Respondent Company was constrained to dismiss the petitioner for his chronic 
absenteeism. The respondent company’s standing orders do not speak about of issue of Show cause notice proposing 
the punishment to be imposed on the delinquent employee. There is no victimization and the punishment of dismissal 
is not harsh and the petitioner was given number of opportunities to correct himself and to be regular to his duties by 
imposing minor penalties. But, he has failed to improve his attendance and resorted to unauthorizedly absent for duty. 
The petitioner’s misconduct compelled the Respondent/Management to impose the penalty of dismissal which cannot 
be termed as unjust. 


3(f). Further, the Respondent Company employs more than 43,600 persons and the production results will depend 
upon the overall attendance and performance of every individual. If anyone remain absent without prior sanction of 
leave or without any justified cause, the work to be performed get effected. Such unauthorized absence creates 
sudden void, which at times is very difficult to fill-up with substitute, and there will be no proper planning and already 
planned schedules get suddenly disturbed without prior notice. For that reason every time the company inform its 
workers to intimate prior to the unit in-charge so that they may arrange substitute and failing to inform will result in to 
production and burden on other employees. The Respondent/Management cannot be held responsible for the alleged 
debts and unemployment and the other allegations of the petition are denied and hence the Respondents prayed to 
dismiss the petition, without granting any relief to the petitioner. 


4. In support of the claim of the Petitioner/‘Workman Ex.W-| to Ex.W-50 and on the other side for the Respondents’- 
Company Ex.M- to Ex.M-6 were marked, with consent. 


5. Arguments of the learned counsel for Petitioner/workman as well as the learned standing counsel for the 
Respondents/ Management heard. Perused the record produced before this Tribunal, their rival arguments and 
citations. 


6. Now the points for consideration are:- 


4 Whether this Tribunal has jurisdiction to entertain this I.D; and whether the domestic enquiry 
conducted by the respondents is held valid or not? 


Whether the charges leveled against the petitioner are proved basing on evidence or not? 


Whether the dismissal order dt.29.08.2025 is liable to be set aside, if so, the petitioner is entitled to 
reinstatement with continuity of service with all attendant benefits and full back wages? 


If not to what relief is the worker entitled to?” 


7. From the pleadings of the Petitioner/Workman and Respondents’ Company, these are the admitted facts that the 
petitioner/ workman worked as Fitter in the Respondents’-Company and he was dismissed from service. Now coming

petitioner to NIMS Hospital, Hyderabad. Ex.W-28 to Ex.W-30 are NIMS Hospital medical prescriptions of petitioner.

documents of both sides are not in much dispute by either side. 


8. Here, the learned standing counsel for the respondents’-company has strenuously argued and raised a Preliminary 
Objection in the Counter that since the coal mining industry is a central subject the Appropriate Government for 
Respondent/ Management is Central Government, which established Central Govt. Industrial Tribunal, at Hyderabad 
for adjudication of Industrial Disputes and the petitioner ought to have approached the said Tribunal for the redressal 
of grievance, if any. But, the Petitioner conveniently avoided filing his petition before the Tribunal established by the 
Central Government and approached this Tribunal; hence it is not maintainable under law and the same may be 
dismissed on this ground alone. 


8(a). The learned standing counsel for the respondents’-company without prejudice to the above preliminary 
objection; has put forth and set forth that the petitioner was appointed as Fitter on I8.2.20I5 and he being an 
underground employee is expected to put minimum (90) Musters in a calendar year. But, he was not regular to his 
duties and did not-in (90) musters from the date of his appointing year to till his dismissal from the services. During 
the year 2022 the petitioner has put-in only (02) musters for which he was issued with charge sheet dt.8.0.2023. If 
he was really suffering from ill health, it becomes his primary responsibility to report sick in Colliery Hospital or he 
should have informed to unit officers about his incapability to attend duties and he would have got leave or loss of pay 
leave but he did not inform anything. The Respondent Company employs more than 43,600 persons and the 
production results will depend upon the overall attendance and performance of every individual. If anyone remain 
absent without prior sanction of leave or without any justified cause, the work to be performed get effected. Such 
unauthorized absence creates sudden void, which at times is very difficult to fill-up with substitute, and there will be 
no proper planning and already planned schedules get suddenly disturbed without prior notice. For that reason every 
time the company inform its workers to intimate prior to the unit in-charge so that they may arrange substitute and 
failing to inform will result in to production and burden on the other employees. 


8(b). The learned standing counsel for the respondents’-company further argued that during the year 20l9 the 
petitioner has put in 6 musters against (90) musters which is less that 0% of attendance, as such the Respondent 
Company was constrained to take action on him by issuing charge sheet for an unauthorized absenteeism under 
Company Standing Order. During the years 2020 and 202], the Petitioner has put in (0) musters and he was charge- 
sheeted vide Charge sheets dt.20.03.202] and 25.07.2022. Further, during the period from January, 2022 to 
December, 2022, the Petitioner has put in 02-musters only. As the above act amounted to misconduct under Company 
Standing Orders, he was issued charge sheet dt.8.0.2023 for absenteeism for the year 2022. Enquiry into the charges 
leveled against the petitioner was conducted by the Enquiry Officer on 0!.09.2023 in which the Petitioner has fully 
participated in the enquiry proceedings. He was given full and fair opportunity to defend his case. In his deposition 
before the Enquiry Officer, the petitioner admitted charges mentioned in the charge sheet. He accepted his mistake 
that he remained absent during the dates mentioned in the charge sheet due to his health problems. However, he did 
not submit any other documentary evidence about the alleged ill-health which prevented him from remaining absent 
from duties during entire absenteeism period. He further admitted that he was imposed punishment of stoppage of 
increment for the year 209; and reversion to lower stage in a time scale by reducing two increments for year 2020 
and 202. As the charges were proved against the petitioner, show cause notice was issued to submit his explanation 
within 7-days on the findings of the E.O. But, he has not submitted any explanation against enquiry findings. Hence, 
the respondents’ company was constrained to impose capital punishment and dismissed from service vide office order 


[भाग I—davs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 555 


dt.29.08.2025. 


8(c). The learned standing counsel for the respondents’-company further put forth and set forth that the petitioner was 
given number of opportunities to correct himself and to be regular to his duties by imposing minor penalties for 209 
to 202. But, the Petitioner has failed to improve his attendance and resorted to unauthorizedly absent for duty during 
the calendar year 2022 also. He failed improve his attendance during the years 2023 to 2025; and even after giving 
opportunities to improve his attendance, the petitioner continued his absenteeism continuously and there is no 
improvement in the attendance. The petitioner’s misconduct has compelled the Respondent/Management to impose 
penalty of dismissal which cannot be termed as unjust. The petitioner not utilized the opportunities given by the 
company and not improved his attendance. Hence, the Respondent Company dismissed him from service vide order 
dt.29.08.2025, which is justified. Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition, without granting any relief to the 
petitioner/workman. 


9. Per contra, on the point of jurisdiction and preliminary objection, the learned counsel for the Petitioner/workman 
has strenuously put forth and set forth that as per the Division Bench Judgment of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 
997(I) LLJ (Supp.)!l, Between: U. Chinnappa Vs. Cotton Corporation of India, this Tribunal has jurisdiction over 
Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., to entertain the Industrial Dispute raised by the petitioner/workman though the 
appropriate Govt. is Central Govt., The petitioner need not raise the Industrial Dispute compulsorily before the Central 
Govt. Industrial Tribunal, Hyderabad alone, as contended by the respondents’ company. Hence, this I.D petition filed 
by petitioner/ workman is well maintainable before this Tribunal for adjudication of the dispute on merits. 


9(a). The learned counsel for the Petitioner/workman further strenuously put forth and set forth that the 
Petitioner/Workman was appointed on 8.2.205 as Fitter. He suffered from chronic ill-health, Heart problem and he 
was imparted prolonged medical treatment in the respondents’ Company Hospitals, Main Hospital, Kothagudem, 
NIMS hospital, Hyderabad and other referral hospitals. But, due to underground work his health was not cured 
completely. He suffered from chronic ill-health, Heart problem and a case of “CAD with S/p CAG-Mild CAD with 
myocardial bridging with Moderate LV dysfunction on medical management with follow up in Neuro Surgery OPD 
i/V/o Cervical Spondylosis with degenerative disc disease and disc bulge”. He was imparted prolonged medical 
treatment in the respondents’ Company Hospitals, Main Hospital, Kothagudem, NIMS hospital, Hyderabad and other 
referral hospitals. But, due to underground work his health was not cured completely. But, alleging absenteeism to 
duties during year 2022, the petitioner was dismissed from service ante-date vide Ref. dt.29.08.2025. Thus, there is 
sufficient and reasonable cause for the petitioner for not attending to duties during the above charge sheet period. But 
without considering the true facts, the respondent No.2 dismissed the petitioner from service, illegally. 


9(b). The learned counsel for the Petitioner/workman further strenuously put forth and set forth that the petitioner 
participated in the enquiry, deposed the true facts of his ill-health. But, the enquiry officer did not properly appreciate 
the facts and he gave his vague findings, which are quite biased and perverse. But, 2 respondent straight away 
dismissed him from service vide Ref. dt.29.08.2025. No prior Show Cause Notice was issued to the petitioner 
proposing the capital punishment of dismissal from service and he was not afforded an opportunity explain as to why 
the extreme punishment of dismissal shall not be imposed on him. The petitioner’s health condition was badly 
deteriorated and he suffered from serious ill health, during the charge sheeted period and there is sufficient and 
reasonable cause for the petitioner for not attending to duties during charge sheet period. 


9(c). | The learned counsel for the Petitioner/workman further put forth and set forth that imposing the capital 
punishment of dismissal from service without any prior show cause notice is against the principles of natural justice. 
The extremely harsh punishment of dismissal is highly excessive and shockingly disproportionate, which amounts to 
economic death of the petitioner. Ever since his dismissal from service, the petitioner is out of employment and could 
not secure any other alternative job in spite of his best efforts. He hails from a very poor family and has no other 
source of livelihood. Therefore, he prayed to set aside the dismissal order and to direct the Respondents’-Company to 
reinstate the petitioner/workman into service with continuity of service, all consequential attendant benefits and full 
back wages. 

POINT '४०.: 

0. Here, on the point of territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal, it is settled Law that as per the Division Bench 
Judgment of the Hon’ble High Court reported in l997(IID)LLJ(Supp.)ll, Between: U. Chinnappa Vs. Cotton 
Corporation of India, this Tribunal has got every jurisdiction to entertain the Industrial Dispute raised by the 
petitioner/workman who was an employee of Singareni Collieries Company Ltd., Even though, the Central Govt. is 
appropriate Govt., for the respondents’-Company, the petitioner need not compulsorily raise the Industrial Dispute 
before the Central Govt. Industrial Tribunal, Hyderabad, as contended by the respondents’ company; and he can file 
this I.D. case before this Tribunal as well. Hence, the contentions of the respondents’-company on the point of 
jurisdiction of this Tribunal are not sustainable under Law. Accordingly, it is answered in favour of the petitioner and 
against the respondents’ Singareni Collieries Company Limited. 


Il. Further in this matter, initially the petitioner/workman denied the validity and legality of the enquiry report. 
But on 20.0.2026, the learned counsel for petitioner filed Memo U/Sec.-A of I.D Act by accepting the procedure 
of domestic enquiry to be fair and valid. Hence, it can be said the Enquiry Officer has followed the principles of 


556 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


natural justice. Now the next question is, whether the misconduct is proved in the facts of the case and the findings are 
not perverse. So, this Tribunal is to re-appreciate the evidence and come to its own conclusion with regard to finding 
guilty or not based on evidence. Accordingly, the Point No.| is answered. 


POINT No.2 & 3: 


2. In view of the pleadings of the Petitioner/Workman as well as Respondents/corporation as well as in view of the 
rival arguments of their respective counsel now this Court will go into the evidence on record. Admittedly, the 
petitioner was dismissed from service by Proc. dt.29.08.2025 wherein it is alleged that the petitioner was absent from 
duty without sanctioned leave or sufficient cause during the year 2022. From a perusal of the record, it shows that 
Charge Sheet dt.l8.0.2023 was issued to the petitioner, which is marked as Ex.M-I3. It is evident from the charge 
sheet that the petitioner absented to duties for 346-days and put-in only 02 actual musters during the year 2022. 
Domestic enquiry was conducted and the enquiry proceedings are marked as Ex.M-4. Further, a perusal of Ex.M-4 
proceedings of enquiry and enquiry report would goes to show that the Petitioner participated in the domestic enquiry 
and deposed that he remained absent on the dates as mentioned in the charge sheet and it was his mistake. He admitted 
that charges and pleaded guilty and deposed that due to his own health problems, he did not attend to his duty. He 
accepted his mistake for remaining absent during the charge sheet year of 2022 and requested to take a lenient view 
for this time and excuse him. He assured that he will put up 20 musters per month and if not, to take action on him. He 
further admitted that he was punished with penalty of stoppage of one increment without cumulative effect for the 
year 209; and reversion to a lower stage in a time scale by reducing two increments 2-times i.e., for the year 2020 
and 202]. 


2(a). From the Enquiry Report which is also under Ex.M-4, it is evident that the petitioner absented to duty without 
sanctioned leave and he accepted the charge made under Company’s standing order 25.25 & 25.3] (Habitual late 
attendance or habitual absence from duty without sufficient cause & Absence from duty without sanctioned leave or 
sufficient cause or overstaying beyond sanctioned leave) mentioned in the charge sheet dt.l8.0!.2023 was held 
proved. The petitioner has not submitted any documents regarding his health problems in the enquiry to substantiate 
his claim. Further, 7-days show cause notice dt.27.0.2023 was issued, which is marked as Ex.M-5 and it appears 
that he failed submit any explanation/representation to the respondents. The dismissal order dt.29.08.2025 is marked 
as Ex.M-l6 wherein it shows that a show cause notice together with a copy of enquiry report and proceedings was 
issued to petitioner, so as to make representation against the findings of enquiry. He acknowledged the same and not 
submitted any representation to it. As the charges leveled and proved being grave and serious, the petitioner was 
dismissed from services of the Company with effect from 0.09.2025. 


3. Apart from the above, the petitioner/workman got marked as many as 50 documents as Ex.W-| to Ex.W-50, which 
include medical prescriptions, medical reports and treatment imparted to him. Most of the medical documents 
submitted by the petitioner/ workman were issued by the SCCL Hospitals, Vasavi Chest & Psychiatric Clinic, Sri Sai 
Cardiac Centre, Vinayaka Neuro Multi Specialty Centre, Suman Gastro & Liver Centre, Purna Laxmi Nuero Centre, 
The Breath Clinic, Sahaja Chest & Surendra Nehru Hospital, MEDICOVER Hospital, PMSSY KMC & several other 
hospitals, which prima-facie show that the petitioner/workman suffered from ill-health from 20!7 to 2025. The 
petitioner explained that due to his ill-health problems, he absented to duties during the charge sheeted year of 2022 
and prayed to consider his case sympathetically. Thus, it is evident from the enquiry proceedings and enquiry report 
under Ex.M-4 as well as the material on record that the petitioner had not put in minimum required musters of 90 
during the year 2022. For which, he submitted that due to his ill-health, he was unable to perform duty regularly 
during the charge sheet period and submitted several medical prescriptions and reports of SCCL and other referral 
hospitals, which are marked as Ex.W-|l to Ex.W-50. Further, the above medical documents of the petitioner lend 
support to his enquiry statement under Ex.M-l4 showing the ill-health suffered by him. These documents clearly 
show that the petitioner/ workman was imparted treatment during the charge sheet period. Hence, the defense put- 
forth by the petitioner is plausible and amount to mitigating circumstances. 


3(a). However, it is clear that the petitioner has not attended to duties during the charge sheet period and the charges 
were amply proved against him. Therefore, it can be said that the respondents/ company has no axe to grind against 
the petitioner. Hence, this Tribunal has no hesitation to hold that the charges leveled against the petitioner/workman 
are proved and misconduct of the workman is established basing on the evidence and the findings of enquiry officer 
are not perverse. But, at the same time much gravity cannot be attributed to the petitioner since his ill-health and 
treatment imparted by SCCL and other referral hospitals is supported by the medical documents, which show 
reasonable cause for the petitioner’s absence during the charge sheet period. 


4. Now the question is whether the punishment of removal from service is disproportionate or not? 


4(a). It is settled law that the object of I.D.Act is to give succor to weaker sections of the society and it is a social 
welfare legislation. Here, there is no “Plumbline Precision” for deciding the proportionality of punishment, which 
depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case. The Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court is empowered to 
exercise discretionary powers U/Sec.ll-A of Industrial Disputes Act for judicious adjudication of the industrial 
disputes. Several factors like nature of duty, past service past conduct, previous penalties if any and the discipline 
required to maintain in the department, victimization and plea of the petitioner/workman and the punishment must be 


[भाग W—davs 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 557 


commensurate with the gravity of charges against the petitioner/workman etc., by considering the relevant factors and 
mitigating circumstances of each case are to be taken into consideration so as to mould the relief appropriately and 
reduce the punishment imposed on the workman. 


5. Here, the learned counsel for the petitioner/workman submitted that the Petitioner was appointed in the year 205 
as Fitter through notification. The petitioner submitted medical documents showing that respondents have referred the 
petitioner to SCCL Hospitals, Vasavi Chest & Psychiatric Clinic, Sri Sai Cardiac Centre, Vinayaka Neuro Multi 
Specialty Centre, Suman Gastro & Liver Centre, Purna Laxmi Nuero Centre, The Breath Clinic, Sahaja Chest & 
Surendra Nehru Hospital, MEDICOVER Hospital, PMSSY KMC & several other hospitals,during the years 209- 
2025. It appears from the said medical documents submitted by the petitioner that he suffered from ill-health, Heart 
problem and a case of “CAD with S/p CAG-Mild CAD with myocardial bridging with Moderate LV dysfunction on 
medical management with follow up in Neuro Surgery OPD iN/o Cervical Spondylosis with degenerative disc disease 
and disc bulge’”’. Further, the petitioner hails from a very poor family, he has got no other livelihood and facing untold 
financial problems, and prayed to consider the case U/Sec.ll-A of I.D. Act. Here, the learned counsel for the 
petitioner relied upon the following citations:- 


|) HON’BLE SUPREME COURT JUDGMENT REPORTED IN AIR [988 SC 303 — Between: Scooter India 
Ltd, Labour Court, Lucknow & ors: 


In this case, the Labour Court while holding that enquiry had conformed to statutory prescriptions and principles 
of natural justice, yet held that order of termination was not justified and ordered for reinstating employee 
with 75% back wages. Wide powers are vested in Labour Court or Tribunal. Labour Court can temper justice 
with mercy and give an opportunity to an erring workman to reform himself. Order of Labour Court granting 
relief of reinstatement with 75% back wages was upheld by Hon’ble Supreme Court. 


2) HON’BLE HIGH COURT JUDGMENT IN W.A. No.0/2008 and W.P.No.767] of 2000, dt.07.04.2009. 
D.B. Judgment: 


In this case, the Labour Court granted reinstatement with continuity of service and half-of back wages. The 
Hon’ble High Court held that since the petitioner remained unemployed from the date of removal, modified 
the award of Labour Court by granting full back wages. 


3) Judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court, dt.24-08-2009 in Civil Appeal No.5762 of 2009, Between: Coal India 
Ltd. & Anr Vs. Mukul Kumar Choudari and others. 


4) Judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court dt.l4-05-2009 Between: Jagadish Singh Vs. Punjab Engineering 
College and others. 


In the above Judgments of the Hon’ble Supreme Court at SI.No.3 & 4 reveals that the punishment should be in 
commensurate with the gravity of the charges and it should not be shockingly disproportionate. Further, this 
Tribunal is adhering to the ratio laid down by their Lordships as applicable to the facts of the present case on hand, 
to the extent of reinstatement only. 


l6. Here, this Tribunal relied on a Division Bench Judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court rendered in Civil Appeal 
No.257/999, dt.08.04.999 between Ajaib Singh vs. Sirhind Co-op. Marketing-cum-Processing Service Society 
Ltd., & another, wherein their lordships held that:- 


“The object of Industrial Disputes Act was to give succor to weaker sections of the society. The emergence of the 
concept of Welfare State implies an end to exploitation of workman and as a corollary to that collective bargaining 
came into it own. The Legislature had intended to protect workmen against victimization and exploitation by the 
employer and to ensure termination of Industrial Disputes in a peaceful manner. 


“The object of the Act, therefore, is to give succor to weaker sections of the society which is a pre-requisite for 
Welfare State. To ensure industrial peace and pre-empt industrial tension, the Act further aims at enhancing the 
industrial production which is acknowledged to be life-blood of a developing society. The Act provides a machinery 
for investigation and settlement of industrial dispute ignoring the legal technicalities with a view to avoid delays, by 
specially authorized Courts which are not supposed to deny the relief on account of the procedural wrangles ”’. 


6(a). Further, in a decision of the Hon’ble High Court reported in 20I2 (l) ALD 220 (DB), wherein their lordships 
observed that:- 


“The Industrial Disputes Act, /947 is a social welfare legislation, which required to be interpreted keeping 
in view the goals set out in the Preamble and Directive principles of State Policy in Part-IV of the Constitution. 
The Labour Court/Industrial Tribunal is conferred with very wide discretion ७/8९८,/7-4 of the Act for granting 
appropriate relief”. 


7. Here, their Lordships of the Hon’ble Gujarat High Court in a case rendered on 04.05.994, Between: Management 
of Glaxo India Ltd., Vs. State of Assam and 3 others categorically observed that “a Labour Court is required to settle 
a dispute according to the principles of natural justice, equity and good conscience and law without attaching 


558 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


undue importance to legal technicalities”. 


8. Further, it is well settled law that if the Industrial Tribunal/ Labour Court is satisfied that the punishment imposed 
on the petitioner/workman is not justified, the Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court is clothed with the power to 
reappraise the evidence in the domestic enquiry and satisfy itself whether the said evidence relied on by the Enquiry 
Officer or Respondents/ Management established the misconduct alleged against the workman. Further, $९८.7/-१ 
comes into effect only at the time when the Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court consider about the punishment to be 
imposed. While previously the Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court had no power to interfere with the punishment, it is 
now clothed with such a power. Apart from the above, Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court should temper justice with 
mercy and not flog the petitioner/workman to asset our might. The power of ocean does not lie in its tumultuous tides 
but in its meditative vastness”. My above view is fortified with the observation of their Lordships of Hon’ble Madras 
High Court in a case Between: High Court of Madras Vs. R.D.Santhana Krishnan बॉ. 2477 December, 2024. 


9. Here, it is to be noted that the concept of Industrial Dispute is quite broad and with the passage of time its horizon 
is being expanded. Further, the disputes are required to be resolved for the purpose of establishing peaceful and 
cordial atmosphere in an industry. Peace and harmony are the quintessential aspects which are to be kept in view 
while dealing with the “/is” or “controversy” relating to any industry. Apart from the above, whether the impugned 
punishment is so disproportionate as to shock the conscience of the Court, has to be decided on the facts of each case, 
having due regard to the gravity of misconduct & nature of duties discharged by the delinquent employee. 


20. Here, it is pertinent to note that the term “misconduct” is the intentional doing of something which the doer knows 
to be wrong, or which he does recklessly, not caring what the result may be. It includes negligence or want of proper 
care which an employee is to take. But, it is a fact that “to err is human” and “to forgive is divine”. Keeping the said 
spirit into consideration and in the interest of cause of justice, every errant conduct of an employee of an organization 
could not be treated as grave misconduct. Further, it is settled law that promoting empathy and understanding by 
encouraging forgiveness, which is a divine quality transcending human limitation, should be preferred to anything else 
in the given circumstances. My above view is fortified by observation of their Lordships of the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court in a judgment rendered Between: Ratilal Jhaverbhai Parmar Vs State Of Gujarat 4.27 October, 2024. 


2. Further, the Hon’ble Madras High Court observed in a case rendered in Management of Hyudai Motor India Ltd 
Vs. T.Sudhakar ... on 377 January, 2022: 


“When scales of justice stands balanced in a given case, the tilt to be exercised should be in favour 
of the poor workmen rather than the mighty Managements.” 


22. Here, I am of the opinion that for promoting ethical behavior and integrity for Public Servants, the Latin Maxim 
(Memento Mori: remember that you must die”) acts as a check against selfish to selfless service. It serves as a 
reminder that: “when office is gone, only the legacy of their character remains”. So, the old Adam or old Man or old- 
self of him or her must die. Otherwise, it will kill them. In summary, Memento Mori serves as a Sobering, yet 
empowering reminder that allows Public Servants to focus on leaving a positive, lasting impact rather than chasing, 
selfish and temporary goals. 


23. Therefore, by taking a holistic view of the matter, I am of the considered view that the extreme punishment of 
removal imposed by the respondents/corporation against the petitioner/workman is harsh, disproportionate and shocks 
to conscience of this Tribunal, hence, deserves to be modified since the disciplinary authority cannot be permitted to 
act arbitrarily and work like a Roman Knight and it cannot be allowed a fight between David and Goliath as in the 
present case on hand. Moreover, facts of this case attracts the proverbial saying “Every saint has a past and every 
sinner has a future” and Biblical proverbs “Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all 
who are destitute” and “Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.” Further, “Heavens 
would not have fallen if one more opportunity is given for the petitioner”. 


24. This Tribunal has perused, analyzed and meditated upon the case at hand, the case laws and principles of law 
referred above. In view of the above facts and circumstances and keeping in view of the principle “temper justice with 
mercy” and to meet the ends of justice, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the punishment of removal from service 
imposed on the petitioner is disproportionate and shocks the conscience of this Tribunal and hence, it deserves to be 
modified appropriately. It appears from the record that the petitioner rendered service of 8-years only in the 
respondents’ company and he is out of employment ever since his dismissal from service. Hence, this Tribunal is of 
the considered view that denial of entire back wages, continuity of service and all other attendant benefits during the 
intervening period from the date of his dismissal to till date and further “Reduction of Pay by TWO Incremental 
stages with cumulative effect” would be a deterrent punishment to the petitioner. However, the past service rendered 
by the petitioner shall be protected and counted for all purposes. Further, the petitioner shall be kept under observation 
for a period six (6) months and in case he commits any misconduct, the respondents’ company is at liberty to take 
stern disciplinary action against him. Hence, the punishment of dismissal from service imposed by the Respondents’ 


[भाग I—daves 30) |] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 559 


Company is hereby modified. Accordingly, the Points 2 & 3 are answered. 


25. IN THE RESULT, the petition is partly allowed. The dismissal order dt.29.08.2025 under Ex.M-6 issued by the 
Respondent No.2 is hereby modified. The respondents’ company is directed to reinstate the petitioner into service, but 
without any back wages, without any continuity of service and without any attendant benefits during the intervening 
period from removal till date and it shall be treated as “not on duty” for all purposes. However, the past service 
rendered by the petitioner shall be protected and counted for all purposes. Further, his Pay shall be reduced by TWO 
Incremental stages with cumulative effect”. Further, the petitioner shall be kept under observation for a period six (6) 
months and in case he commits any misconduct, the respondents’ company is at liberty to take stern disciplinary 
action against him. The petitioner is entitled to the salary only from the date of publication of the Award. Copy of the 
Award be sent to the appropriate Government for publication. Both parties shall bear their own costs.

PARTIES: Rajesh Ghosh 
(dependant son of Late Dulal Ghosh) 
Vs.

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (l) and sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, !947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-2202/78/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 0.08.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Central Kajora Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“Whether the action of the management of Central Kajora Colliery, Kajora Area, M/s. E.C.Ltd. in not 
providing employment on compassionate ground to Sri Rajesh Ghosh dependent son of Late Dulal Ghosh, 
Ex- SDL Operator, UM NO. 776237 and in not paying monetary compensation to Smt. Rina Ghosh wife of 
Late Dulal Ghosh under the provisions of NCWA is fair, legal and justified? If not, what relief the dependent 
of deceased workman is entitled to? ” 


| On receiving Order No. L-2202/78/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 0.08.2022 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on l0.08.2022 and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2; Rajesh Ghosh, dependant claiming employment and monetary compensation on account of Late Dulal 
Ghosh has appeared in person. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative filed a petition on behalf of the union praying 
for withdrawing the case on the ground stated therein. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for Eastern Coalfields Limited 
is present. 


3. It is submitted by Mr. Kumar that dependent of Late Dulal Ghosh had sought for compassionate employment 
on account of legal death of Dulal Ghosh. It is further submitted that prior to his disappearance in the year 2009, Dulal 
Ghosh was dismissed from service in the year 2006 on account of his unauthorized absence for a short period. In this 
Industrial Dispute dismissal of Dulal Ghosh has not been challenged as such it would not be appropriate for the 
dependent to proceed with his claim for compassionate employment in place of his father. Considered. No objection is 


[भाग ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 563 


raised. It appears to me that claim made by the union for providing compassionate employment to Rajesh Ghosh is 
contingent upon findings as to whether Dulal Ghosh was terminated in a proper manner or not. Since no dispute has 
been raised relating to the manner of dismissal of Dulal Ghosh, present Industrial Dispute cannot find logical 
conclusion. Industrial Dispute is therefore dismissed for non-prosecution. Let a No Dispute Award be drawn up. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed for non-prosecution. A No Dispute Award be drawn up in the above 
Reference case. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government 
of India, New Delhi for information and Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERJEE, Presiding Officer

AWARD 

On failure of conciliation before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Raniganj at Durgapur on 
02.08.2022 and in exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (.) and sub-section (2A) of Section 0 
of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
Order No. L-2202/80/2022-IR(CM-ID) dated 29.08.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Madhusudanpur Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 

“Whether the demand of Koyla Mazdoor Congress (HMS) vide their letter dated 24.05.2079 against the 

action of the Management of Madhusudanpur Colliery, Kajora Area, M/s. E.C. Ltd. in not giving promotion 

to Sri Utpal Chakraborty, in Cat-V from Cat-IV as Electrician per cadre scheme is fair, legal and justified? 

If yes, what relief the workman concerned is entitled to? ” 

| On receiving Order No. L-2202/80/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 29.08.2022 from the Government of India 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 29.08.2022 / 
0.09.2022 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear 
and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 
2. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate appeared for the management of Eastern Coalfields Limited. Mr. Rakesh 
Kumar, union representative, appearing on behalf of Utpal Chakraborty and filed an application praying for closing 
the case on the ground that the concerned employee who raised this dispute for getting promotion from 
Category-IV to Category-V as an Electrician has superannuated from service. It is stated in the petition that he does 
not want to proceed further in this case. Copy served upon learned advocate for the management. On a perusal of 
record, it appears that the case is fixed up today for appearance of the workman and further evidence of workman 
witness. 

3. On repeated calls at 2.50 PM Utpal Chakraborty is not found present. Mr. Kumar moved the application for 
disposing the case. Considered the application. It appears that the aggrieved workman has already retired from service 
and no purpose would be served by continuing the case before this Tribunal. The Industrial Dispute is accordingly 
disposed of for non-prosecution. Application filed by the union representative is disposed of. Let a No Dispute Award 
be drawn up in the light of my above findings. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on consent. Let a No Dispute Award be drawn up in the above 
Reference case. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government 
of India, New Delhi for information and Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERIEE, Presiding Officer

5. Based on the rival pleadings placed before this Tribunal my learned predecessor framed the following issues 
for trial on 09.09.204 as follows : 
“I. Whether the Domestic Enquiry conducted by the Respondent against the Applicant is fair and 
proper? 
2. Whether the Order of discharge passed by the Respondent Management against the Applicant 
w.e.f. 24.0].20I3 is void ab initio for not obtaining approval from this Tribunal in view of the

the Applicant?

6. Based on the above pleadings Issue No. | was treated as preliminary issue and the matter came to be 
posted for Evidence of II Party. Both sides adduced evidence and the preliminary issue stood answered in the 
affirmative on 08.08.209 holding that the enquiry held against the I Party by the II Party is fair and proper 
and the matter was posted for Argument. On 07.02.2020 I party filed an application under Section of ID Act 
seeking permission to adduce evidence and filed an affidavit in lieu of his examination in chief and sought 
permission to produce documents in support of the allegations made in the affidavit. While so it is reported 
before this Tribunal that the I Party workman Sri Susainathan expired and the matter was posted for taking 
steps to implead his legal representatives. Despite having afforded ample opportunities no legal representatives 
of the I Party workman did come on record, the matter was then heard on behalf of the management. 
7. Eventually the Argument advanced by the II Party is heard in detail. 
8. Issues No. । and 5: The history of the case narrated above clearly indicates that the I Party could not 
pursue the case subsequent to the submission of his claim statement due to his untimely death. Though he was 
represented by his counsel until then, subsequent to his death the learned counsel did not take any effective 
steps to bring the legal heirs of the deceased workman on record. So literally this Tribunal is incapacitated to 
put on record any valid case of the I Party workman to be controverted by the contesting II Party. 
9. The factum of death of the I Party is seen recorded on 28.02.2025 as informed by the learned counsel 
for the I Party. Copy of the death certificate is not forthcoming from the side of the I Party. As already 
observed, no legal heirs have come on record to prosecute the case anymore. So much so, necessarily the claim 
stands abated as necessary steps have not been taken in time to implead the legal heirs / legal representative of 
the late workman or any steps to condone the delay in impleading the LRs and to set aside abatement of the 
claim. In this scenario this reference is to be answered as the claim stands abated as the I Party workman died 
long ago without the matter being persued by any of the legal representatives. Hence, the following award. 
AWARD

Government hereby publishes the Award (Reference. 29/2023) of the Central Government Industrial Tribunal-

and their workmen, received by the Central Government on 06/03/2026.

REFERENCE CASE NO. 29 OF 2023 


PARTIES: Manoj Kumar Pati 
Vs. 

Management of Madhusudanpur Colliery, Kajora Area of M/s. ECL 
REPRESENTATIVES: 
For the Workman: Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress. 
For the Management of ECL: Mr. P.K. Das, Advocate. 
INDUSTRY: Coal. 
STATE: West Bengal. 
Dated: 0.42.2025 


AWARD 


The above named workman being represented by President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress raised an Industrial 
Dispute before the Dy. CLC(C), Asansol through Samadhan portal dated 0.0.2023. The contention of the union is 
that Manoj Kumar Pati, a General Mazdoor bearing U.M. No.l02066 was posted at Madhusudanpur Colliery, Kajora 
Area. By order dated 09.08.203, Manoj Kumar Pati was deployed to perform the duty of attendance clerk at 
Madhusudanpur Colliery but after rendering continuous service for a long period, the management of ECL refused to 
regularize his service as attendance clerk. A conciliation proceeding was held which resulted in failure. The 
Government of India through the Office of the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), Asansol issued Order 
No. (0)/2023/E. dated 22.05.2023 whereby in exercise of powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section () and sub- 
section (2A) of Section 0 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947) referred the scheduled dispute for 
adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“ Whether the action of the management of Madhusudanpur Colliery, Kajora Area, M/s. ECL in not paying 
the amount of differencial wages and not regularisation to the post of Attendance Clerk to Sri Manoj Kumar 
Pati is justified or no ? If not, what relief the workman is entitled to”. 


l. On receiving Order No. (40)/2023/E. dated 22.05.2023 from the Office of the Deputy Chief Labour 
Commissioner (Central), Asansol, Ministry of Labour, Government of India, for adjudication of the dispute a 
Reference case was registered on 30.05.2023 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through 
registered post, directing them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support 
of their claims. 


2; Manoj Kumar Pati filed written statement on !3.09.2023 through Koyala Mazdoor Congress. The facts which 
unfolded from the written statement is that Manoj Kumar Pati, a permanent employee of ECL was posted as General 


568 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


Mazdoor. Subsequently he was deployed as attendance clerk against permanent vacancy for managing attendance of 
the employees at Madhusudanpur Colliery. He performed his duty continuously till initiating this Industrial Dispute. It 
is contended that the workman requested the management to pay him difference of wage of Clerk Grade-II and the 
amount which was being paid to him as a General Mazdoor in Cat-I. The aggrieved workman also requested the 
management for regularizing him in the post of Clerk but the management of ECL did not consider his request. 
Further case of union is that according to the Memorandum of Settlement dated 02.08.203, Manoj Kumar Pati was 
deployed as attendance clerk but the management did not pay him the wages of Clerical Grade-lII. It is asserted that 
the management regularized number of workers as Clerk without any test or examination. It is submitted that 
Ramakant Yadav, Sudip Mitra, Bhakta Das Badyakar, Ramawadh Bouri of the same colliery were regularized as clerk 
without undergoing any test or examination. Accordingly, Manoj Kumar Pati, who performs service in the capacity of 
clerk for ten years without any promotion should be regularized to the post of clerk as per the provision of Certified 
Standing Order of the company, which lays down that if a worker performed any particular job continuously for a 
period of three months or above, he should be regularized to that post. It is further ascertained that management of 
Madhusudanpur Colliery have the requirement of attendance clerk and Manoj Kumar Pati fulfills all the requirements 
for the post of clerk, as such he should be regularized to that post and should be paid difference of wages from the 
date of his working as a clerk. 


3. Management of ECL contested the case by filing written statement on !3.09.2023. The version of the 
management is that the post of attendance clerk comes under Clerical Grade as it is a centralized post. Selection to 
clerical post is done by the ECL Headquarters and for this purpose notifications are issued from time to time for filling 
vacancy in the post. Candidates having requisite qualification are required to apply for this post and they are selected 
for clerical posts only after they qualify in the selection test conducted by the management. Therefore, the workman is 
not entitled to be regularized to the post of clerk unless he fulfills certain criteria. It is admitted by the management 
that the Manoj Kumar Pati has been placed to manage attendance work at colliery Pit No. 7 vide Office Order No. 
MSP/6/689 dated 09.08.20I3. It is further stated that in case of encadrement/regularization of a workman from 
General Mazdoor Cat-I to Clerk Grade-III, no incremental benefit is given if the prevailing basic of the General 
Mazdoor is more than the minimum basic of Clerk Grade-III. If the prevailing basic of the concerned workman is less 
than the minimum basic of Clerk Grade-III, then the workman is given the benefit by fixing his pay at minimum basic 
of Clerk Grade-III. Displaying a chart, showing comparative basic pay of Manoj Kumar Pati and the minimum 
monthly basic of Clerk Grade-III from the year 20l3 to 2023, Management claimed that basic pay of Manoj Kumar 
Pati since 20l3 was already more than the minimum basic pay of Clerk Grade — III. As such no difference of wage is 
payable to the workman and the workman is not entitled to any outstanding dues. It is urged that Manoj Kumar Pati 
was never regularized to the post of Clerk Grade -III and he is not entitled to any benefit claimed. 


4. The central point for consideration is whether Manoj Kumar Pati, a General Mazdoor, deployed as 
attendance Clerk should be regularized to the said post and whether he is entitled to payment of any difference of 
wages. 


5. Union examined Manoj Kumar Pati as WW-l. He filed an affidavit-in-chief and claimed that in a 
Memorandum of Settlement dated 02.08.20l3, management agreed to place him as attendance clerk along with other 
workman and Office Order No. MSP/6/689 dated 09.08.20I3 was issued. The witness further averred that the 
management received the benefit of service rendered by him for several years but did not place him in Clerk Grade-II 
and did not pay him difference of wages between General Mazdoor and Clerk Grade-II. The workman claimed that he 
completed one year of service as attendance clerk on 0.09.204 and should be paid the wage of Clerk Grade-II w.e.f. 
0.09.204. In respect of the comparative chart showing statement of wages from 20l3 to August 2023, the workman 
claimed that he had been performing the job of Clerk Grade-II and the basic pay of Clerk Grade-II should have been 
taken into consideration instead of Clerk Grade-III. The workman witness further stated that the management of 
Kajora Area as well as other areas of ECL had sent the names of other employees of ECL for regularization who were 
deployed to work in clerical jobs and the competent authority of ECL approved the proposal of their regularization. It 
is urged that the regularization process should also be considered with consistency but the management adopted pick 
and choose policy according to their wish, ignoring legitimate claims. 


During examination-in-chief, the workman produced the following documents: 
(i) Copy of identity card is produced as Exhibit W-|. 
(il) Copy of Office Order dated 09.08.203 produced as Exhibit W-2. 
(iii) Copy of Memorandum of Settlement in Form ‘H’ dated 02.08.203 is produced as Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) Copy of application dated 9.05.207 submitted to Personnel Manager for regularization as 
attendance clerk is produced as Exhibit W-4. 


(५) Copy of application dated 3.09.202] for regularization as attendance clerk is produced as Exhibit

Exhibit W-7.

(ix) Copy of proposal dated 06.05.209 initiated at Colliery level for regularization of Manoj Kumar Pati 
to the post of Attendance clerk is produced as Exhibit W-9. 


It appears from his examination in chief that Manoj Kumar Pati was initially appointed at Kalidaspur Colliery, ECL 
and he came on transfer to Madhusudanpur Colliery in 2004. After he was placed as attendance clerk on the basis of a 
settlement dated 02.08.20I3 (Exhibit W-3), the workman submitted an application dated 9.05.20!7 before Personnel 
Manager for his regularization to the post of attendance clerk (Exhibit W-4). He submitted another application for his 
regularization as attendance clerk (Exhibit W-5). He produced a copy of Office Order dated 2.0!.20l! whereby 
similarly placed workers were regularized in their respective posts where they were deputed to work. Copy of Office 
Order dated 2.0i.20l! has been produced as Exhibit W-6. The workman produced a copy of Memorandum of 
Settlement where the management agreed to pay difference of wages on regularization (Exhibit W-8). Thereafter, a 
proposal dated 06.05.209 was initiated at the Colliery level regarding regularization of Manoj Kumar Pati to the post 
of attendance clerk (Exhibit W-9). The workman claimed that at present he receives a daily wage of Rs. 27I3.5] per 
day but could not state the difference of wages he would be entitled to if regularized. In cross-examination, the 
witness denied that in all cases before posting in clerical grade, a selection procedure has to be carried out. Workman 
denied that for regularization in clerical grade, the preconditions which have to be fulfilled are educational criteria and 
participation in the selection process. Witness deposed that in many cases, persons have been posted in clerical cadre 
without any selection test. It transpires from his testimony that he was not aware about the notifications of 05.06.204, 
.02.206 and 02.02.208 issued by the management for holding written examination for the post of Clerical Grade- 
III. The witness was unable to state if other employees of the establishment applied for the post of clerical grade. The 
witness admitted that if his basic pay was computed on the basis of daily wage @ Rs. 273.5 for twenty six days, his 
basic pay would be more than starting pay in the post of attendance clerk. 


6. Mr. Proloy Dasgupta, management witness filed an affidavit-in-chief admitting the factual aspects. The 
witness has clearly stated in paragraph 4 of the affidavit that the post of attendance clerk is a centralized post and 
selection to clerical grade is carried out by ECL Headquarters. It is stated that notifications are issued from time to 
time according to vacancy in the post and candidates having requisite qualification apply for the post and their 
selection to the post of clerical grade is considered only after qualifying in the selection test. The aggrieved workman 
not having fulfilled such requirements do not qualify to be regularized to the post of clerk. The witness stated that in 
case of regularization from General Mazdoor Cat-I to Clerk Grade-III, no incremental benefit is given if the basic of 
the concerned workman aspiring for the post in Clerk Grade has a higher minimum pay than the basic pay of Clerk 
Grade-I. The witness further deposed that since 20l3, Manoj Kumar Pati was already receiving more than the 
minimum basic of Clerk Grade-II, he is not entitled to any difference of wage or any outstanding dues. 


In course of his examination-in-chief, the management witness produced the following documents: 


(i) Copies of notifications dated 05.06.20I4, .02.206 and 02.02.208, inviting applications for Clerk 
Grade-III are produced as Exhibit ७-।, Exhibit ४-/2 and Exhibit M-I/3 respectively. 


(il) Copy of service book of Manoj Kumar Pati is produced as Exhibit M-2. 
(iil) Copy of Office Order dated 09.08.20I3 is produced as Exhibit M-3. 
(iv) Copy of Memorandum of Settlement in Form-H is produced as Exhibit M-4. 


(५) Copy of letter dated 29.0.20l7 informing Manoj Kumar Pati of vacancies in Clerical post is 
produced as Exhibit M-5. 


(५) Copy of comparative salary chart of Manoj Kumar Pati as General Mazdoor Cat-I and Clerk Grade- 
III is produced as Exhibit M-6. 


(vil) Copies of payslips of Manoj Kumar Pati from 203-2024 are produced as Exhibit M-7. 


(viii) Copies of Office Orders dated 6.06.203 and .0.2020 granting SLP to Manoj Kumar Pati are 
produced as Exhibit M-8 and M-8/I. 


(ix) Copy of attendance statement of candidates appearing for Clerk Grade-III Exam is produced as 
Exhibit M-9.

(xi) Copy of notification dated 02.02.20I8, inviting applications for Clerk Grade-III is produced as 
Exhibit M-I. 


(xii) Copy of Office Order dated 25.04.20I9 by which 2 candidates of ST, 22 candidates of SC and 7 
candidates of general category were selected in the post of clerk grade-III is produced as

Exhibit M-2. 


During cross-examination, the management witness deposed that Ramakant Yadav and Ramawadh Bouri were 
regularized as Store Clerk Grade-III from their earlier post of Clerk Grade-III on the basis of recommendation of 
Departmental Promotion Committee. It transpires from further cross-examination of MW-| that the aforesaid persons 
did not apply in response to any notification and their selection was not through any test. So far as circulation of 
notification is concerned, the witness stated that it was displayed on the Notice Board and no separate notice were 
issued to eligible candidates. It may be gathered from the cross-examination of management witness that Manoj 
Kumar Pati is functioning as attendance clerk from the year 20l3 without interruption. The witness also admitted that 
Manoj Kumar Pati is matriculate and he served for more than three years in the post of attendance clerk. The witness 
admitted that apart from holding test there is process for selection by fulfillment of educational qualification as well as 
length of service of candidate and he is also required to undergo an examination held by the management. The witness 
deposed that Ramakant Yadav and Ramawadh Bouri were regularized to Clerk Grade-III in the year 20l] on the 
recommendation of departmental promotion committee/selection committee of ECL headquarters but the witness was 
unable to state if any test was held for their regularization to the post of Clerk Grade-III. A suggestion was put to 
management witness by the union representative that Ramakant Yadav and Ramawadh Bouri were regularized to the 
post of Clerk Grade-III without any examination or appearing in a test which the witness denied. No specific 
document was thereafter produced by the management to establish that examination was held for regularization of the 
two workmen in clerical grade. 


de Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative argued that Manoj Kumar Pati was placed as attendance clerk on 
the basis of a Memorandum of Settlement. He performed satisfactorily in the said capacity for several years, since 
August 203 but the management of ECL did not considered his application for regularization to the post and no 
difference of pay has been granted in favour of the workman for the duties performed by him. It is argued that Manoj 
Kumar Pati is a matriculate. It is argued by the union representative that several other workmen from other Collieries 
have been deployed and then regularized as Clerk without undergoing any selection process or any examination. In 
the instant case, the workman has been functioning against a vacant post and the management should regularize him in 
the said post and paid his dues towards difference of pay for the work done by him as attendance clerk. 


8. P.K. Das, learned advocate for the management strenuously argued that initially the workman was placed at 
Pit No. 7 of Madhusudanpur Colliery to manage the attendance work w.e.f. 09.08.20I3 on the basis of Memorandum 
of Settlement but he was never posted as a clerk and he is not entitled to the benefit of being regularized or being 
granted the difference of pay between the post of Clerk Grade-III and General Mazdoor unless he applied against a 
notification issued from time to time to fill such post. Only after appearing in the selection test and on being 
recommended by the Departmental Promotion Committee, an employee can be posted in the clerical grade. 


9, I have considered the rival arguments in the light of facts and circumstances of the case disclosed in the 
pleadings and evidence adduced by both parties. It is abundantly clear that Manoj Kumar Pati who was initially posted 
as a General Mazdoor on 09.0.2004 (Exhibit W-), was deployed to function as an attendance clerk from 09.08.203, 
on the basis of an Office Order produced as Exhibit W-2. It appears from the record that Memorandum of Settlement 
under section!2(3) of Industrial Disputes Act, 947 was executed on 02.08.20I3 by representatives of the union and 
the management wherein it was agreed before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (Central), Raniganj that Manoj 
Kumar Pati would be placed to manage attendance work at Madhusudanpur Colliery. Copy of Form ‘H’ has been 
produced as Exhibit W-3. Though Manoj Kumar Pati claimed that he was placed as attendance clerk, both the 
Memorandum of Settlement dated 02.08.20l3 and Office Order dated 09.08.20I3 disclose that he was placed to 
manage the attendance work at Madhusudanpur Colliery and certainly it was not any placement order as attendance 
clerk. The workman has been continuously rendered service in the capacity of attendance clerk since 09.08.203. The 
concerned workman made several representations before the Manager (Personnel) and Agent, Madhusudanpur 
Colliery seeking his regularization to the post of attendance clerk. Copies of applications dated 9.05.20I7 and 
3.09.202] have been produced as Exhibit W-4 and W-5 respectively. On 06.05.20l9, a proposal was made for 
regularization/encadrement of two employees namely Manoj Kumar Pati and Subhas Sahana, Switch Board attendant 
to the post of Clerk Grade-III. A copy of the proposal signed by the Deputy Manager (Personnel) has been produced 
by the union as Exhibit W-9. From the aforesaid documents, it is affirmed that the management of ECL was fully 
conscious that Manoj Kumar Pati is functioning as Clerk Grade-III and that he proposed for his regularization. 
Workman has produced copy of Office Order dated 2.0.20I at Exhibit W-6 which reveals that on recommendation 
of Departmental Promotion Committee constituted at the headquarter level, the competent authority upon 
recommendation of Departmental Promotion/Selection Committee constituted at headquarter level regularized 
Ramakant Yadav and Ramawadh Bouri as Clerk Grade-III. The management witness in his cross examination dated 
06..2024 deposed that Ramakant Yadav and Ramawadh Bouri Clerk Grade-III were regularized as Clerk Grade-III 
on recommendation of Departmental Promotion Committee and further stated that their selection was not based on 
any test. It is therefore manifestly clear that management of ECL while regularizing some of its employees to the post 
of clerical cadre did not issue any prior notification and the concerned persons without applying against any 
notification and without appearing in any examination were recommended to fill up clerical posts. 


0. Mr. Das has produced copies of notification dated 05.06.20I4, .02.20l6 and 02.02.20l8 which are 


[भाग W—davs 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 57] 


notifications for the written examination for selection to Clerk Grade-III from eligible departmental candidates. Manoj 
Kumar Pati in his evidence stated that he was not informed about such circulars. According to the management, if a 
person from a lower cadre is placed to function as a clerk, he would not be entitled to any difference of pay if the basic 
pay of the person so deployed is more than the minimum basic pay of Clerk Grade-III. It has been argued that Manoj 
Kumar Pati was receiving higher pay than the minimum pay of Clerk Grade-III. Therefore, he is not entitled to get 
difference of pay. In the instant case, the aggrieved workman has rendered continuous service as attendance clerk for 
ten years without being regularized to the post. The management has relied upon a scheme for Ministerial Staff in the 
general Clerical Cadre which has been circulated vide II No. 34 dated 7.07.984. For the purpose of being designated 
as Clerk Grade-III, the required minimum qualification is matriculation or any equivalent examination from any 
recognized Board of Examination and he would be eligible for promotion to the post of Clerk Grade-II by the 
recommendation of Departmental Promotion Committee. In the instant case, it would appear from the written 
statement and affidavit-in-chief of management witness that in the year 20l3, Manoj Kumar Pati was receiving a 
higher basic pay as General Mazdoor than the minimum basic pay of Clerk Grade-III. Since 09.08.203, the workman 
has rendered continuously served as attendance clerk of Madhusudanpur Colliery. Admittedly, the aggrieved 
workman is a matriculate. ॥५४-] in his cross-examination has admitted that Manoj Kumar Pati is a matriculate and he 
has served for more than three years as attendance clerk. By dint of such educational qualification and experience he 
is already receiving a basic pay higher that Clerk Grade-III. Manoj Kumar Pati is found eligible for his regularization 
to the post of Clerk Grade-II immediately on completion of three years in the clerical post. Therefore, he is entitled to 
be regularized to the post Clerk Grade-II w.e.f. 09.08.20I6. There is preponderance of evidence to prove that 
regularization of subordinate staff members to clerical grade of the management were considered on the basis of their 
educational qualification and experience without holding any examination or separate selection process. The case of 
Ramakant Jadhav and Ram Awadh Bouri clearly indicate that they were regularized to the post of Clerk Grade-II 
without any selecting procedure. The management should certainly strive to bring about a parity in treatment of its 
employees. I therefore hold that Manoj Kumar Pati is entitled to be regularized to the post of Clerk Grade-II and is 
entitled to difference of wage between Clerk Grade-II and pay received by him w.e.f. 09.08.20l6 and disburse the 
dues in respect of the difference of pay in the post of Clerk Grade-II w.e.f. 09.08.206 within a period of three months 
from communication of this order. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


The Industrial Dispute is allowed in part against the management of ECL. Manoj Kumar Pati be regularized 
to the post of Clerk Grade-II w.e.f. 09.08.206 and he shall also be entitled to receive difference of pay for the post of 
Clerk Grade-II w.e.f. 09.08.206. Management of ECL shall complete the entire procedure within three months of 
communication of this order. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of 
India, New Delhi for information and Notification.
