AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, !947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-2202/76/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 03.08.2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Khas Kajora Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“Whether the demand of the President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress (HMS), Asansol in his letter dated 
26/6/2027 (copy enclosed) to reinstate in service to Sri Rabila! Majhi. U.G. Loader, who was dismissed vide letter 
No. KA:PM:C-6:0:3369/24 dated 2/0०7//9965(८०779 enclosed) against the action of the management of Khas Kajora 
Colliery, Kajora Area, M/s E.C.Ltd. in their letter No. KKC/P&IR/C-6/Re-State/33l dated 72/26/2077 (copy 
enclosed), is proper, legal and justified? If yes, what relief the workman concerned is entitled to? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/76/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 03.08.2022 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0.08.2022 and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2, Rabilal Majhi, the dismissed workman filed written statement in this case on 27.03.2023 through 
Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress. In gist, the fact of the case as disclosed in their written 
statement is that Rabilal Majhi was a permanent employee and posted as an Underground Trammer, bearing U.M. No. 
552834 at Khas Kajora Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). 
Rabilal Majhi could not attend his duty w.e.f. December 993 due to his illness. The management of ECL issued 
Charge Sheet against him on 23.05.994. After recovery from illness the workman reported for his duty but he was 
not allowed to join. Management issued Charge Sheet bearing No. KKK/P&IR/C-6/I9/94 dated 23.05.994. The 
Charge Sheet was not served upon Rabilal Majhi as it was sent to his home address while he was residing at the 
Colliery. Management conducted ex-parte enquiry against the workman without service of Novice of enquiry and he 
was dismissed from service of the company on the basis of the order of dismissal bearing No. KA:PM:C- 
6:0:3369/2 dated 09.0.996. It is contended that no second Show Cause Notice was served upon the workman 
and the management of ECL imposed a disproportionate and harsh punishment upon the workman without complying 
settled law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, which provides that a second Show Cause Notice should 
be issued to the workman before the final order of punishment is passed if the Enquiry Officer and Disciplinary 
Authority are not the same person. According to the workman the Enquiry Officer should have ensured service of 
Charge Sheet and Notice of enquiry before holding ex-parte enquiry and a second Show Cause Notice and Enquiry 
Proceeding with findings ought to have been served upon the workman before the order of dismissal was issued. Non- 
compliance of such procedure gives rise to breach of natural justice and a punishment of dismissal from service due to 
absence from duty for a period of five months and twenty-two days is disproportionate to the alleged misconduct. It is 
urged that the ex-parte order of dismissal is liable to be set aside and the workman should be reinstated in his service 
with full back wages since the date of his dismissal. The workman also submitted that according to the Memorandum 
of Settlement dated 22.05.2007 a dismissed workman had the right to submit mercy appeal which was to be forwarded 


[भाग —avs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 573 


by the colliery and Area management to the ECL Headquarters for consideration and if the period of absence from 
duty was less than nine months and the age of the workman was below forty-five years, management had assured to 
consider the mercy appeal. Since the workman’s representation in the form of mercy appeal was not considered the 
present Industrial Dispute had to be initiated, seeking reinstatement with back wages. 


3 Management of ECL contested the case by filing written statement on 30.0!.2023. Management admitted 
that Rabilal Majhi having U.M. No. 552834 was posted as an Underground Trammer and was a permanent employee 
of Kahs Kajora Colliery under Kajora Area of ECL. According to the management the workman was a habitual 
absentee. On several occasions he remained absent from duty and lastly, he remained absent from December 993 
without any information or authorization. After a long unauthorized absence, the management of ECL issued a Charge 
Sheet to the workman bearing No. KKK/P&IR/C-6/9/94 dated 23.05.994 under Clause 7(/)(n) of the Model 
Standing Orders applicable to the Coal Mine Industries. A domestic enquiry was initiated and the Enquiry Officer 
issued two Notice of enquiry dated 25..995 and .2.995. The workman did not attend the enquiry nor did he 
send any information on any of the dates as such the enquiry was conducted ex-parte on 20.2.995. In course of 
enquiry the charge of unauthorized absence was fully established against the charged employee. He was dismissed 
from his service by order of dismissal bearing No. KA:PM:C-6:0:3369/2 dated 09.0.996, issued by the General 
Manager, Kajora Area, ECL. The past record of the workman relating to his attendance was not satisfactory and he 
attended duty only on 9 days out of 306 days in the year 992, 48 days out of 305 days in the year 993 and nil out 
of 305 days in the year 994. According to the management absenteeism is a serious misconduct and it hampers the 
work and production process of the employer. According to the management ample opportunity was provided to the 
workman to improve his performance and attendance but he did not mend his conduct as a result he was dismissed 
from service on the charge of unauthorized and habitual absence. The management in support of their case relied upon 
a decision of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta in the case of Dayanand Paswan Vs. Coal India Limited and 
Others [Writ Petition No. 874 of 204], wherein the action of the management of ECL in dismissing the workman 
was held to be justified and in the said judgement the Hon'ble High Court emphasized that the employee must take his 
duty seriously and cannot take his employment for granted. He must follow the rules and regulation of the employer 
company and must conduct himself in a disciplined manner and perform his duties with responsibility not only for 
personal excellence but also for collective good of the organization which he serves. Management further asserted that 
the punishment of dismissal of the workman from service is proportionate to the nature of misconduct of long 
unauthorized absence. It is urged that the workman is not entitled to any relief and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be 
dismissed. 


4. The moot point for consideration is whether the demand for reinstatement of Rabilal Majhi, Underground 
Loader in his service after his dismissal on 09.0.996 is legal and justified. 


5 The union examined Rabilal Majhi as Workman Witness No. | and filed his affidavit-in-chief. It is stated in 
the affidavit-in-chief that he could not attend his duty as he fell sick since December 993. After his recovery he 
reported for duty but was not allowed to join. The management issued Charge Sheet bearing No. KKK/P&IR/C- 
6/9/94 dated 23.05.994 which was sent to his home address. He did not receive the Charge Sheet as he was residing 
at the Colliery at the relevant time and the Notice was returned to the management undelivered. The workman further 
averred that he visited the colliery and met the Manager and requested him to allow him to join duty. It is further 
stated that the Enquiry Officer conducted enquiry and without ensuring service of Notice of enquiry concluded the 
enquiry proceeding. The General Manager of Kajora Area on the basis of recommendation made by the Agent 
awarded the punishment of dismissal against the workman and issued order bearing No. KA:PM:C-6:0:3369/2 
dated 09.0.996. It is also stated in the affidavit-in-chief that for absence from duty for five months and twenty-two 
days, from December 993 to 22.05.994 the management should not have awarded such harsh punishment of 
dismissal which is disproportionate to the nature of misconduct. According to the workman there has been violation of 
principles of natural justice by debarring him from appearing in the enquiry and by not issuing second Show Cause 
Notice. It is claimed that the order of dismissal is illegal and as he was below forty-five years at the relevant time and 
his period of absence was only five months and twenty-two days, he should have been reinstated in service in terms of 
Memorandum of Settlement dated 22.05.2007. During his examination-in-chief the workman produced the following 
documents : 


(i) Photocopy of Chargesheet dated 23.05.994 issued against Rabilal Majhi is produced as Exhibit ४४-।). 
(0) Photocopy of letter of dismissal dated 09.0.996, as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) photocopy of the application of Rabilal Majhi, praying for mercy and reinstatement of duty, as Exhibit 
W-3. 


(iv)Photocopy of another application of Rabilal Majhi for re-instatement, as Exhibit W-4. 


(v)Photocopy of the letter issued by the Personnel Manager, Kajora Area dated 2.0.20I, stating as Rabilal 
Majhi had absented for more than nine months, his case was not fit for recommendation for re-instatement, as 
Exhibit W-5. 


574 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


The workman further deposed that he was suffering from jaundice and reeling of head but he was unable to produce 
any document relating to his medical treatment during the period of his absence from duty. He further deposed that he 
did not take part in the enquiry proceeding and he used to reside at Shyamla which is thirty kilometers from Beldanga. 


6. In cross-examination the witness stated he did not submit any reply to the Charge Sheet and for the first time 
during evidence he stated that he could not attend his duty from December 993. He admitted in his cross-examination 
that in his prayer for reinstatement submitted on 30.2.200 the statement made by him in the prayer was correct. It 
appears from Exhibit W-3 that he was prevented from attending duty on being tortured by some money lenders. 
Suggestion was put to the witness that he intentionally remained absent from duty as he was not eager to work but the 
witness denied the same. 


7. Management examined Mr. Proloy Dasgupta, Manager (Personnel), Khas Kajora Colliery, ECL as 
Management Witness No. |. In his affidavit-in-chief he stated that Rabilal Majhi, ex-Underground Trammer was a 
habitual absentee for which he was previously reprimanded on several occasions. The workman again remained 
absent from December !993 without any authorization or information to the appropriate authority. He was 
chargesheeted under Clause |7()(n) of the Model Standing Orders. The matter was referred for domestic enquiry and 
two Notice of enquiry were issued on 25..995 and I.2.995. The workman did not attend the enquiry on any of 
the two dates and the domestic enquiry was proceeded ex-parte where the charge levelled against the workman was 
proved. The General Manager thereafter issued a letter dated 09.0.996 dismissing the workman on the said charge. 
It is sated that the workman attended duty for only !9 days out of 306 days in the year 992, 48 days out of 305 days 
in the year 993 and nil out of 305 days in the year 994. The management witness averred that absenteeism is a 
serious offence as it hampers the work of the employer and production process. Concerned workman was given 
several opportunities to improve his performance in respect of his physical attendance but he did not improve his 
conduct. The management therefore cannot maintain the name of the workman on roll for indefinite period. 
Accordingly, he was dismissed. Management claimed that the punishment meted out to the ex-workman is 
proportionate to the nature of his misconduct and claimed that the management is justified in dismissing the ex- 
workman from the service of the company and the workman is not entitled to any relief. In course of his evidence 
management witness produced the following documents: 


(i) Photocopy of the Charge Sheet dated 23.05.994 issued to the workman is marked as Exhibit M-I. 
(ii) Photocopy of the letter of appointment of the Enquiry Officer dated 20..!995, as Exhibit M-2. 


(iil) Photocopies of two Notice of Enquiry dated 25.!.995 and .2.995 addressed to Rabilal Majhi, as 
Exhibit M-3 and M-4 respectively. 


(iv) Photocopy of the Enquiry Proceeding in which workman did not participate, as Exhibit M-5. 
(५) photocopy of Enquiry Report along with findings of the Enquiry Officer, as Exhibit M-6. 


(५) Photocopy of letter of dismissal dated 09.0.996 issued by the General Manager, Kajora Area, as 
Exhibit M-7. 


The witness deposed that he has no document to show that the Notice of enquiry was served upon the workman. 
Management witness admitted that no second Show Cause Notice was issued to the workman nor any copy of the 
Enquiry Proceeding was supplied to him before dismissal. 


8. In cross-examination management witness deposed that he was unable to state how Charge Sheet and Notice 
of enquiry was served upon the workman. He admitted that he is unable to state the mode of communication of 
Charge Sheet and Notice of enquiry to the workman before commencement of enquiry. It is also evident from the 
cross-examination that no second Show Cause Notice was served upon the workman before dismissal of the workman 
from service and denied that the punishment of dismissal is not proportionate to the misconduct. The management 
witness conceded the fact that the mercy petition of the workman was not considered. 


9. Heard argument advanced by Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative who submitted that the management 
of ECL has dismissed the workman in violation of principles of natural justice and without complying the mandate of 
the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Union of India and Others Vs. Mohd. Ramzan Khan [AIR 
(99) SC 47]] and the Circular issued by the Coal India Limited, where it is provided that a second Show Cause 
Notice is required to be served upon the workman giving him an opportunity to submit his explanation in respect of 
the findings against him, specifically in the case where the Enquiry Officer and Disciplinary Authority are different 
persons. Mr. Kumar further argued that the nature of punishment is harsh and disproportionate as the workman who 
was below forty-five years of age at the relevant time and absented only for a period of five months and twenty-two 
days was not reinstated on the basis of his representation and appeal though in the Memorandum of Settlement dated 
22.05.2007 the management has agreed to consider the cases where the period of absence is less than nine months and 
the age of the charged employee is less than forty-five years. It is stated that the workman should be reinstated in 
service of the company and he should be paid full back wages. 


0. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management, in reply argued that the workman joined in service on 


[भाग IVS 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 575 


3.0.99] and he was habitual absentee from the very beginning. From the records maintained by the employer 
company it would appear that since his joining he was a habitual absentee and he was reprimanded on several 
occasions for improving his attendance but he performed duty only for 29 days since his joining. The workman 
deliberately remained absent from December 993 and did not return. Charge Sheet was issued to the workman which 
he was fully aware of but he has not participated in the enquiry after two Notice of enquiry were issued to him. The 
workman in course of adducing evidence in this Industrial Tribunal has admitted the fact that he remained absent from 
duty since December 993 till Charge Sheet was issued to him and has deposed that at the relevant time, he used to 
reside at Shyamla which is thirty Kilometers from Beldanga. In his examination-in-chief the witness deposed that he 
was suffering from jaundice but he admitted that he has no medical treatment papers and did not lead evidence in 
support of his illness. Learned advocate referred to the cross-examination of Workman Witness No. | and argued that 
the witness admitted in his prayer for reinstatement submitted on 30.2.20l0 (Exhibit W-3) that he was unable to 
attend duty on being harassed by money lenders. Therefore, it is urged that there was no treatment papers in support of 
workman that he was suffering from illness. Learned advocate strenuously argued that the workman deliberately 
remained absent without any reason and is not entitled to any relief. 


ll. I have perused the materials on record and considered the rival arguments. It appears to me that the workman 
did not perform his duty seriously and sincerely. It is an admitted fact that he remained absent for more than five 
months without any authorization. The workman failed to produce any medical papers in support of his plea of illness. 
In the affidavit-in-chief the workman stated that after recovery from illness he reported for duty but was not allowed 
to join. He did not mention any date when he reported for duty. The workman was fully aware about issuance of 
Charge Sheet and in paragraph no. (5) of the affidavit-in-chief he stated that when Charge Sheet was issued, he was 
in the Colliery and the Charge Sheet was sent to his native place. It can well be assumed that when a person is 
performing his duty, he will be available in the colliery and during his absence he would be at his registered address 
provided in the Service Record. Though the workman was fully aware that management had issued Charge Sheet 
against him which was sent to his native village during his long absence, he did not bother to find out the indictment 
in the Charge Sheet. Management witness produced a copy of Charge Sheet as Exhibit M-land copies of Notice of 
enquiry as Exhibit M-3 and M-4. Copy of the Enquiry Proceeding is produced as Exhibit M-5 and Report of the 
Enquiry Officer is produced as Exhibit M-6. The workman has been found guilty for his absence from duty from 
9.4.993 to 20.2.995, which is more than two years which covers the entire period of his absence disclosed in the 
Charge Sheet from December 993 to 23.05.994. It is abundantly clear from the findings of the Enquiry Officer that 
the workman never showed up for duty for more than two years. It is true that the management of the employer 
company is duty bound to observe the principles of natural justice before dismissing its employee from the service of 
the company by issuing a Charge Sheet, Notice of enquiry and holding a proper enquiry proceeding. Management 
made best effort by issuing such Charge Sheet and Notice at his native place. However, this duty cast upon the 
management is not absolute in the absence of reciprocal responsibility of the employee to attend his place of work and 
either to inform the reason of absence or to seek authorization for leave on any acceptable ground. The duty of 
observing principles of natural justice by the employer has been complied and no prejudice is caused to the workman. 
In a case where the workman abandoned his duty for a long period without any information, he cannot be allowed to 
challenge the act of the management as violative of natural justice. In the instant case the management issued a 
Charge Sheet and appointed an Enquiry Officer. The Enquiry Officer in turn issued two Notice of enquiry and fixed 
two dates. The workman did not participate in the enquiry and remained absent on being chased by the money lenders, 
as disclosed in Exhibit W-3. The management after initiating a domestic enquiry on May 994 ultimately issued the 
order of dismissal on 09.0.!996. On a perusal of the order of dismissal (Exhibit W2/M-7) it appears that two Notice 
of enquiry were served upon the workman at his home address under registered post and enquiry was held on 
20.2.996 but the workman did not participate. In my considered view no prejudice was caused to the workman by 
non-issuance of second Show Cause Notice. It further appears to me that after dismissal of the workman in January 
996 the workman raised the Industrial Dispute on 26.06.202l, before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), 
Raniganj, Durgapur. There has been a delay of more than twenty-five (25) years in raising the Industrial Dispute after 
dismissal of the workman. The circumstances revealed that the workman has not acted in a diligent manner and his 
prayer for reinstatement after such a long period of silence is of no merit. I therefore, hold that the demand made by 
the union for reinstatement of the dismissed workman is not legally tenable and the Industrial Dispute merits dismissal 
on contest. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. Rabilal Majhi, the dismissed workman is not entitled to 
any relief of reinstatement and back wage. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the 
Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and 
Notification.

AWARD 


On failure of Conciliation the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, in exercise of powers 
conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 
(4 of 947), vide its Order No. L-2202/09/2023-IR(CM-ID) dated 0.02.2023 has referred the following dispute 
between the employer, that is the Management of Bhanora West Block Colliery, Sripur Area of M/s. Eastern 
Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred as ECL) and their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


[भाग I—davs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 577 


“ Whether the demand of President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress (HMS), Asansol vide letter dated 24/07/2022 
(copy enclosed) against the action of the management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields in relation to its Bhanora West 
Block Colliery under Sripur Area in regretting the claim of employment of Sunny Mejhan, dependent daughter of Late 
Binodi Mejhan, Ex-Earth Cutter, UM No. 20888 vide their letter No. ECL/CMD/C-6B/EMPL/WD-6698/20/233 dated 
44/70/2020 (copy enclosed), is proper, legal and justified? If yes, what relief Sunny Mejhan, dependent daughter of 
the deceased workman concerned is entitled to and what directions are necessary to the Management in this 
respect? ”. 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/09/2023-IR(CM-II) dated 0.02.2023 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case No. of 2023 was registered on 
0.02.2023 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear 
and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims and a list of witnesses. 


2. Union filed written statement on !7.05.2023 in support of the case of Sunny Mejhan, dependent daughter of 
Binodi Mejhan, ex-employee of ECL. The fact of the case in brief is that Binodi Mejhan was posted at Bhanora West 
Colliery as Earth Cutter. She died in harness on 30.08.2009 leaving behind Sunny Mejhan as her dependent and 
unmarried daughter. Sunny Mejhan gave death information to the management of Colliery on 09..2009 and 
submitted an application on 28.2.2009 praying for employment in place of her deceased mother. After receiving the 
death information, the employer company did not ask for any document required for processing her prayer for 
employment. After preparing various documents like Attestation Form, Relationship Certificate, No Objection 
Certificate of other family members, Indemnity Bond and affidavit, some time was taken for submitting those 
documents. The management of the employer company sent the proposal for her employment to the Area level for her 
screening and medical examination. The IME Board held examination and declared her fit for employment and also 
assessed her age as 35-40 years. Proposal for employment was forwarded to the Headquarter of ECL for approval. 
The Headquarter of ECL again sent Sunny Mejhan for her medical examination by Apex Medical Board, where her 
age was assessed as 40-45 years as on 3!.08.2020 and she was declared unfit for employment due to over age. 
According to the union, Sunny Mejhan was below 35 years on the date of death of her mother. As per age assessed by 
the IME Board and also the second assessment of age, it is clatmed that on the date of submitting her application, she 
was below 35 years of age. According to the union, the age of the dependent should be considered as on the date of 
application and not on the date of holding medical examination. Further contention of the union is that the 
management should not have assessed the age of Sunny Mejhan for the second time, as the age decided once by the 
IME Board should be taken as final if the same was not challenged by the claimant. Union asserted that the age of 
Sunny Mejhan was 28 years |! months and 29 days on the date of death of Binodi Mejhan and if management 
accepted the result of second age assessment, her age would be 3] years 6 months and 2 days on the date of death of 
Binodi Mejhan. The dependent daughter it is urged is entitled to employment. The union has challenged the decision 
of ECL management which regretted the claim for employment of Sunny Mejhan describing the decision as wrongful 
and illegal. It has been prayed that Sunny Mejhan, the unmarried daughter of Binodi Mejhan should be provided 
employment as per the provisions of NCWA with all other consequential benefits. 


3 Management of ECL contested the case by filing written statement on 04.04.2023 refuting the claim of the 
dependent daughter of ex-employee. It is disclosed that on the basis of application dated 24.05.204 submitted by 
Sunny Mejhan, she was asked to appear before the IME for assessment of her fitness for work. Her IME was held on 
3.03.208 which assessed her age as 35-40 years and was declared medically fit for employment. According to the 
management, the Area authority conducted IME at the Area level which was contrary to Circular No. 994 dated 
6.03.20!7 which provides that if a proposal of employment is made after expiry of two years of death, the same 
should be sent to the Headquarter of the company. Accordingly, ECL Headquarter forwarded the case of Sunny 
Mejhan to CMS (IC), ECL Headquarter for determination of her age. After medical examination, the age of Sunny 
Mejhan was assessed to be 40-45 years on 3.08.2020. On the basis of medical examination, Chief Manager 
(Personnel), Sripur Area communicated the decision of the competent authority by his letter no. GM/SA/C- 
6D/7/2020/I24 dated 03..2020 that Sunny Mejhan is not eligible for employment as per provisions of NCWA and 
therefore, the competent authority regretted the claim of employment of Sunny Mejhan. In course of time, this 
decision was communicated to Sunny Mejhan by letter dated 27..2020. On 23.2.2020, the dependent daughter 
prayed for review of the decision. The Assistant Personnel Manager, Sripur Area, in response to the review 
application informed that as Sunny Mejhan was above 35 years on the date of her application for employment, the 
same was rejected. Management asserted that there is no merit in Industrial Dispute and the same is liable to be 
dismissed. 


4. In order to substantiate their case, union examined Sunny Mejhan as WW-I. She filed her affidavit-in-chief 
stating that after death of her mother on 30.08.2009, she informed the management on 09.I.2009 and claimed 
employment as a dependent of her mother by submitting an application on 28.2.2009. She admitted that IME Board 
decided her age as 35-40 years on 3.03.208 and later on 3!.08.2020 the Apex Medical Board decided her age as 40- 
45 years and declared her unfit due to being over age. It is averred that once she accepted the age assessed by IME on 
3.03.20I8, her age should not have been assessed by the Apex Medical Board and the Medical Board could have 


578 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


decided her physical fitness due to gap of 2 years from IME. It is claimed that according to the age assessed as 35-40 
years on 3!.03.208, her age should be computed as 37.5 years on that date and she was 28 years 0 months 29 days 
on the date of death of her mother on 30.08.2009. She further claimed that as per assessment of her age by IME Board 
held at Sanctoria on 3.08.2020, her age should have been calculated as 3] years 06 months on the date of death of her 
mother and on the date of application, her age was 3! years !0 months which is within the qualifying age limit. 
During examination-in-chief, the witness produced the following documents: 
(i) Copy of identity card of Binodi Mejhan is produced as Exhibit W-. 
(il) Copy of death certificate of Binodi Mejhan is produced as Exhibit W-2. 
(iil) Copy of death registration certificate of Binodi Mejhan is produced as Exhibit W-3. 
(iv) Copy of death certificate of father of Sunny Mejhan (husband of Binodi Mejhan) is produced as 
Exhibit W-4. 
(५) Copy of service excerpt of Binodi Mejhan is produced as Exhibit W-5. 
(vi) Copy of Office Order dated 9.02.20I0 for deleting the name of Binodi Mejhan from the company’s 
roll after being informed of her death by her daughter is produced as Exhibit W-6. 
(vil) Copy of letter dated 3.08.2020 calling Sunny Mejhan to appear before IME Board is produced as 
Exhibit W-7. 
(viii) Copy of IME report of Sunny Mejhan dated 3].08.2020 is produced as Exhibit W-8. 
(ix) Copy of letter dated 4.0.2020 regretting the prayer of employment of Sunny Mejhan is produced 
as Exhibit W-9. 
(x) Copy of letter dated 03.]].2020, informing Sunny that she was not found eligible for employment is 
produced as Exhibit W-0. 
(xi) Copy of application dated 23.2.2020 submitted by Sunny Mejhan for review of decision taken by 
management is produced as Exhibit ४४-।|. 
(xii) Copy of letter dated 05/06.04.202! wherein Area Personnel Manager rejected Sunny Mejhan’s 
prayer for review is produced as Exhibit W-2. 
(xiii) | Copy of Aadhar Card of Sunny Mejhan is produced as Exhibit ४७-3. 
From her cross-examination, it transpires that Binodi Mejhan left behind two daughters, namely Sunny Mejhan and 
Malati Murmu and one son namely Jogindra Majhi. She further stated that her younger brother has expired. She 


denied the suggestion that she did not submit any application to the Manager, Bhanora West Block Colliery on 
28.2.2009 claiming employment in place of her mother. 


5. Mr. Ranveer Rathour has been examined as MW-I. He deposed that the the competent authority found 
Sunny Mejhan was not eligible for employment as pe the provision of NCWA for being over age and this decision has 
been communicated to her on 27..2020. 

In course of his examination-in-chief, the management witness produced the following documents: 


(i) Copies of application dated 24.05.20l4 submitted by Sunny Mejhan praying for compassionate 
employment, is produced as Exhibit M-]. 


(il) Copy of IME report of Sunny Mejhan dated 3!.03.208, is produced as Exhibit M-2. 


(iil) Copy of letter dated 20/23.09.20l9 furnishing clarifications and information sought by the 
Headquarter, is produced as Exhibit M-3. 


(iv) Copy of letter dated 03..2020 informing Sunny Mejhan that she was not found eligible for 
employment, is produced as Exhibit M-4. 


(५) Copy of second IME report of Sunny Mejhan dated ३].08.2020 is produced as Exhibit M-S. 


(५) Copy of application dated 23.2.2020 submitted by Sunny Mejhan for review of decision taken by 
management is produced as Exhibit M-6. 


(vil) Copies of letter dated 02.0!.202 forwarding the application to competent authority for review is 
produced as Exhibit M-7. 


(viii) Copy of letter dated 05/06.04.202] wherein Area Personnel Manager rejected Sunny Mejhan’s 
prayer for review is produced as Exhibit M-8. 


In course of his cross-examination, the management witness deposed that in Office Order dated 200 it is mentioned 
that date of death of Binodi Mejhan was informed on 09..2009. The witness deposed that the management informed 
the dependents of their rights and entitlements in respect of the service of Binodi Mejhan. The witness also deposed 
that the age of Sunny Mejhan was assessed between 35 years to 40 years as on 3.03.20I8 and she was less than 35 


[भाग I—aves 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 579 


years on the date of submission of application. 


6. The point of contention in this case is whether the management of ECL is justified in regretting Sunny 
Mejhan’s claim for employment as dependent of her mother Binodi Mejhan. 


7. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative advancing his argument submitted that after the death of Binodi 
Mejhan, her daughter informed the management about the death of her mother by letter dated 09..2009, which will 
be evident from Office Order dated 9.02.20l0 (Exhibit W-6). After deleting the name of Binodi Mejhan from the 
Roll of the company, management did not disclose the rights of the dependents in respect of the service of Binodi 
Mejhan. Initially, an application was submitted by the dependent daughter on 28.2.2009 claiming employment but it 
took some time to prepare some documents which were filed in 20l4. Mr. Kumar argued that the management held 
IME of Sunny Mejhan on 3.03.208 at the Area level where her age was decided as 35-40 years. On the basis of such 
age determined by the IME Board, the age of Sunny Mejhan was 3] years 06 months on 28.2.2009, the date of 
submitting her application for employment which was well within the upper age limit of 35 years. It is argued that 
though no dispute was raised by Sunny Mejhan against age assessed by the management a second age assessment was 
held on 3.08.2020 where her age was determined to be 40-45 years and according to such assessment, her age was 3] 
years 0 months on the date of death of her mother. The union representative strenuously argued that the dependent 
daughter is eligible for employment in place of her deceased mother as per provisions of NCWA. 


8. Mr. P.K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL in reply argued that no claim for employment 
was made by the dependent daughter until 24.05.20l4. The management of the company assessed the age on 
3.03.20I8 as 35-40 years and subsequently the Apex Medical Board on 3.08.2020 assessed the age as 40-45 years 
which implies that her age was more than 35 years on the date of submitting her application for employment on 
24.05.204. Learned advocate argued that management communicated the decision of the competent authority to the 
dependent daughter that she was not found fit for employment for being over age. 


9. Considered the arguments in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case, pleadings submitted, 
evidence adduced and the guiding rules. Admittedly, Binodi Mejhan, the mother of Sunny Mejhan died in harness on 
30.08.2009. According to the provisions of clause 9.3.4 of NCWA, the dependents to be considered for employment 
should be physically fit and suitable for employment and the age should not be more than 35 years. In the case of 
Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 2024] the Hon'ble 
Division Bench of High Court at Calcutta observed : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is a 
settlement under section 2 (9) of the Industrial Disputes Act, /947 and has binding effect on the parties thereto under 
section 76 (3) of the Act of 7947. NCWA has made provisions for compassionate appointment for the dependents of 
the deceased employee. ” 


Clause 9.3.2 of NCWA-VI provides that employment would be provided to one dependent of the workman who dies 
while in service. Furthermore, Clause 9.3.4 provides that the dependents to be considered for employment should be 
physically fit and suitable for employment and their age should not be more than thirty-five (35) years provided that 
the age limit for a female spouse would be forty-five (45) years as given in Clause 9.5.0. On a close reading of 
provisions of NCWA, there is no specified time for reckoning the age of dependent for considering him/her for the 
purpose of employment. In this matter, a Circular has been issued by the management of ECL bearing No. CIL/C- 
58/83८/9.4.3/63 dated 25.07.2003 wherein it has been provided that the age on the date of submitting the 
application would be considered for offering employment on compassionate ground. Union produced a copy of an 
application, said to have been submitted by Sunny Mejhan on 28.!2.2009 addressed to the Manager, Bhanora West 
Block Colliery. The document has been marked ‘X’ for identification and it bears a receiving seal without mentioning 
the designation of the person who received it. The management of ECL claimed that application for employment was 
submitted by Sunny Mejhan for the first time on 24.05.20l4. Therefore, it needs to be considered whether the 
dependent daughter was within the age limit of 35 years on 24.05.204. 


0. The process for considering the proposal for employment was initiated as per the guidelines of the company 
and medical examination of Sunny Mejhan by the IME at the Area level was held on 3.03.20I8. The IME Board 
found her fit for employment and her age was assessed as 35-40 years on that date. Once again, she was examined by 
the Apex Medical Board on 3.08.2020 where her age was assessed as 40 to 45 years as on 3.08.2020. It has been 
contented on behalf of the management that as there was delay of more than two years in raising the claim for 
employment after the death of employee. As per circulars of ECL dated 6.03.207, IME was to be held at Sanctoria 
Hospital. Therefore, the determination of age at the Area level is not to be taken into consideration. It is urged that age 
determined by the Apex Medical Board at Sanctoria Hospital had to be relied upon and on the basis of such 
determination, the age of Sunny Mejhan was 42 years, 6 months on 3!.08.2020. Accordingly, her age on 24.05.20I4 
was 36 years, 3 months. The contrary argument of the union was that the age of Sunny Mejhan in the Service Excerpt 
report of her mother dated 0.04.987 was recorded as 7 years. Therefore, on basis of such document, the age of 
daughter would be 34 years, | month and 24 days as on the date of submitting her application on 24.05.204. It may 
be further gathered from the argument of the union that once the age of the dependent daughter was assessed at the 


580 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


Area Level on 3!.03.208 and found her 35 to 40 years of age, by computing her age on the date of application, she 
would be 33 years and 8 months of age and well within the age limit for providing employment to her. I find that once 
the age was determined by the IME at the Area Level on 3.03.208 and no complaint was raised against such 
findings by the candidate, management was estopped from reassessing the age of the candidate by another Medical 
Board by the Headquarter after a period of two years and five months only to disqualify her on the ground that she 
was over age. Management appears to have delayed the process to frustrate the cause. Management cannot approbate 
and reprobate their own act to disable a person from securing her right. Therefore, I am not inclined to accept the 
subsequent age assessment of Sunny Mejhan after a lapse of two and a half years only to contradict management’s 
own finding on earlier occasion which was in favour of the candidate. Union has produced a copy of letter bearing No. 
ECL/CMD/C-6B/GM (P&IR)/2022/633 dated 2.05.2022 issued by the General Manager (P&IR), ECL addressed to 
the General Managers of Sripur and other Areas laying down guidelines for pre-employment medical examination, 
wherein it is stated that their earlier communication dated 6.03.20l7 about holding IME at Sanctoria Hospital in 
respect of cases which are beyond two years from the date of death of ex-employee stood withdrawn and henceforth 
IME of all cases would be exclusively held at the Area according to its cluster as was done before, and therefore, there 
is no need to send any person to Sanctoria Hospital for holding their IME. On a perusal of the guidelines, I find that 
though it was issued in May 2022, much after holding the second IME at the Headquarters level, the management of 
ECL was possessed with the idea of holding all IME at the Area Level instead of at the Headquarters. In view of such 
guidelines dated 2.05.2022 which was issued during pendency of this Industrial Dispute, I am of the considered view 
that the age assessed by the IME Board at the Area Level on 3.03.20I8 needs to be considered as the report 
determining the correct age of Sunny Mejhan. The decision of the competent authority relying upon the subsequent 
findings of the Apex Medical Board, contradicting the earlier assessment is found self-defeating and has no 
foundation. Thus, the same is not sustainable under the law. 


Il. This Industrial Dispute has been raised due to disqualifying Sunny Mejhan for her employment. It is found 
that the age of the dependent daughter according to the Service Excerpt of the employee and the first assessment by 
the IME brings her within the zone of consideration, so far as age is concerned. She was also found fit for 
employment. Therefore, the afterthought of the management followed by a second medical examination of the 
candidate two and a half years after her first IME is prejudicial, arbitrary, illegal and cannot be accepted. Under 
NCWA, there is no time limit for submitting application by the dependent of the deceased employee for employment 
and it is well settled in case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others (supra). 
On the basis of my above discussion, Sunny Mejhan is entitled to employment under the management of ECL against 
the death of her mother, Binodi Mejhan. The management of ECL is directed to complete the procedural formalities 
for her employment within a period of two months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


The Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Bhanora West Block Colliery, ECL. 
This Industrial Dispute is decided in favour of union with a direction to the management to provide employment to 
Sunny Mejhan, the dependent daughter of Binodi Mejhan under the employer company by completing all procedural 
formalities within two months from the date of communication of this Award. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be 
sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, !947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-2202/45/202-IR(CM-II) dated 0.0.202l has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Parascole Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“ Whether the action of the Management of Parascole Colliery under Kajora Area of M/s. Eastern Coalfields 
Ltd. in regretting the claim for employment of Shri Guddu Rabidas, dependent son of Late Dukhi Rabidas, Ex-Pump 
Operator of Parascole Colliery is just and legal? If not, to what relief the dependent son is entitled to? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/45/202-IR(CM-II) dated 0.!0.202! from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0I.0.202] and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 

on Koyala Mazdoor Congress, representing the dependents of the deceased employee, Dukhi Rabidas, filed 
written statement / claim statement on 29.2.202l. The facts disclosed in the written statement of the union is 
that Dukhi Rabidas was posted as a Pump Operator at Parascole Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields 
Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). He died in harness on 3.05.20I5 at Central Hospital, Kalla. After his death 
Chunni Devi, the wife of the deceased employee, as head of the family of the deceased nominated Guddu Rabidas 
their younger son for providing employment by the ECL as a dependent. The management of the company issued a 
letter, asking for relevant documents and “No Objection” Certificate (hereinafter referred to as NOC) from the other 
legal heirs. The union disclosed in the written statement that Dukhi Rabidas died leaving behind his wife Chunni 
Devi, three sons namely, Umesh Rabidas, Ramavali Rabidas and Guddu Rabidas and four daughters. Chunni Devi 
submitted a NOC in favour of Guddu Rabidas by all other legal heirs of Dukhi Rabidas. Subsequently, Umesh 
Rabidas, the elder son changed his stand and raised objection against the prayer for employment of Guddu Rabidas. 
The management of ECL on the basis of such objection stopped processing the prayer for employment and proposed

son lives separately therefore the objection raised by Umesh Rabidas cannot be a reason for the management not to 
provide employment to the younger son. The present dispute has been raised by the union, praying for providing 
employment to Guddu Rabidas according to the provision of National Coal Wage Agreement (hereinafter referred to 
as NCWA) and also to pay monetary compensation to the widow till employment is provided to Guddu Rabidas.

MMCC on enhanced rate as per NCWA instead olaying claim for employment. According to the management in order

mentioned that no objection from all the family members of the deceased employe, appearing in the Service Record is 
essential. It is contended that the Industrial Dispute raised is misconceived and not maintainable. 

oyee. Due to such discrepancies in the Service Record the objection raised by Umesh Rabidas, management of ECL

ll. In the cross-examination the management witness deposed that after prayer for employment, the management

I2; Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative, arguing for the dependent son submitted that soon after the death of 
Dukhi Rabidas on I3.05.205, Guddu Rabidas, the younger son submitted an application informing death of his father 
(Exhibit W-3) and Chunni Devi, the widow prayed for providing employment to Guddu Rabidas (Exhibit W-4). 
Referring to the Standard Operating Procedure of Coal India Limited dated 28.08.2023 which was duly approved in 
the 63" CMDs meeting held on 8.08.2023, it is submitted that the time limit for submitting application for 
employment was relaxed by extending such time up to 3! December 2023 and thereafter from the year 2024 the time 
limit for submitting application was only for one year from the date of death. It is argued that in the instant case 
application has been filed on 03.08.207, therefore there was no reason for not considering the application on the 
ground of delay in submission. Mr. Kumar further argued that Chunni Devi, the wife of the deceased employee being 
the head of the family had nominated Guddu Rabidas, the youngest son for employment in place of the deceased 
employee. According to the union representative the widow has the prerogative to decide as to who amongst the 
family members should get employment in place of her deceased husband. It is argued that if the widow had the right 
to decide the claim for employment of dependent, any objection raised by other siblings against the nominated 
dependent would be without force. It is urged that the management of ECL is under legal obligation to provide 
employment to Guddu Rabidas, the dependent and nominated son of the deceased employee as per the provisions of 
Clause 9.3.] of NCWA. 


3. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL, in reply argued that Umesh Rabidas, the eldest 
son of the deceased employee raised objection against the proposal for employment to his younger brother, Guddu 
Rabidas. It is argued that according to the Circular dated 3.0.2009 issued by the General Manager (P&IR), ECL it is 
essential that all the dependent members of the deceased employee, whose names appeared in the Service Record 
must submit no objection in favour of the person seeking employment. In the instant case Umesh Rabidas raised 
objection against the nomination of Guddu Rabidas, as such the management offered to pay MMCC to the widow of 
the deceased. It is further argued that due to such objection raised by another son of the deceased employee the prayer 
for employment of Guddu Rabidas is not sustainable and the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


4. Having considered the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties, the pleadings, evidence adduced and 
the provisions under Clause 9.3.l of NCWA-IX, I find that employment has to be provided to one dependent of the 
employee who died while in service of the company. In Clause 9.3.3 of NCWA-IX a dependent has been described 
for this purpose as a wife or a husband as the case may be, son and legally adopted son. It does not specify that the 
eldest son of the deceased employee should be considered for employment. The other essential criteria for providing 
employment as per Clause 9.3.4 of NCWA-IX is that the dependent who is considered for employment should be 
physically fit, suitable for employment and aged not more than 35 years provided that the age limit in case of female 
spouse would be 45 years as given in Clause 9.5.0. There is no dispute over the fact that Dukhi Rabidas died in 
harness on 3.05.20I5, leaving behind Chunni Devi, his widow, three sons namely, Umesh Rabidas, Ramavali 
Rabidas, and Guddu Rabidas and four daughters namely Gouri Devi, Pravila Devi, Manita Devi and Kanchan Devi. 
From the evidence on record, it is clear that Chunni Devi nominated her youngest son for employment as a dependent 
in place of her deceased husband. The application was initially submitted by her on 03.08.207 (Exhibit W-4). The 
management in response to her letter issued letter No. 096 dated 09/I.0.207 (Exhibit W-5), requesting her to 
submit complete employment file with “No Objection” from all the dependent family members as per Clause 9.4.0 of 
NCWA-IX. It is admitted by the management that on !5.0.2020 Guddu Rabidas submitted all the documents along 
with application of Chunni Devi and “No Objection” from other family members (Exhibit W-7). The management of 
ECL having received such application should have acted upon the same by considering the prayer for employment. It 
has been argued on behalf of the management that Umesh Rabidas, the eldest son of the deceased employee submitted 
an objection against the prayer for employment (Exhibit W-8/M-6) due to which management was unable to consider 


[भाग Ive 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 585 


the prayer for employment. On a close reading of the provision of Clause 9.4.0 of NCWA-IX, I found that there is no 
mandatory requirement of submitting NOC by all the family members of the deceased employee in favour of the 
dependent claiming employment. In the instant case Chunni Devi, the principal dependent of the deceased employee 
has clearly stated in her affidavit-in-chief, supporting the case of the union in their written statement that Umesh 
Rabidas was not a dependent and was living separately from the family of the deceased employee. It is also gathered 
from the evidence of Guddu Rabidas that Umesh Rabidas was running a business in the style of General Store at his 
native place, which has been established. Such evidence has not been controverted. Therefore, the management is 
dutybound to consider the option exercised by the dependent of the deceased employee and not impose their view of 
providing alternative relief of MMCC, which is usually opted by the spouse when she is more than forty-five years of 
age and has no dependent to take up employment on behalf of the family of the deceased. In the instant case all four 
married daughters of the deceased employee as well as the widow have expressed their support in favour of Guddu 
Rabidas, seeking employment as a dependent of their deceased father. The management of Parascole Colliery is not in 
a position to dispute the claim on the ground of delayed submission of application for employment as there has been a 
relaxation of time limit up to 3.2.2023 for submission of application as per the Standard Operating Procedure under 
NCWA dated 8.08.2023. The evidence on record clearly brings out the fact that Guddu Rabidas, the younger son has 
been nominated by the widow of the deceased employee who is the principal dependent and reposed faith upon the 
dependent son as a person who would take care of family responsibilities and did not support the objection raised by 
the other two sons, namely Umesh Rabidas and Ramavali Rabidas. In view of the fact and circumstances of this case I 
hold that the management is under a legal obligation to consider the prayer for employment of Guddu Rabidas as a 
dependent son of Dukhi Rabidas as per the provisions of Clause 9.3.l of NCWA-IX and complete the employment 
procedure within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest in favour of Guddu Rabidas, the dependent son of the 
deceased employee Dukhi Rabidas. The management of Parascole Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields 
Limited is directed to consider the prayer for employment of Guddu Rabidas and complete the employment procedure 
within two (2) months from the date of communication of the Award. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above 
findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for 
information and Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERJEE, Presiding Officer

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section l0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, !947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-2202/08/2023-IR(CM-II) dated 3.0!.2023 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Lachipur Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“ Whether the demand of President, Koyala Mozdoor Congress (HMS), Asansol vide letter dated /4/07/2022 
(copy enclosed) against the action of the management of Lachipur Colliery, Kajora Area of M/s. Eastern Coalfields 
Ltd. over denial of employment on compassionate ground to Sri Dhapru Das dependent son of Late Ch. Jagu Das, Ex- 
U.G.Loader, U.M.No.56890], violating the provisions of NCWA vide Order No. ECL/CMD/C-6B/EMPL/ED- 
409076/27/29 dated 7/2.02.2027/ and subsequent Order No. ECL/CKC/P&IR/C-6/202I/55] dated 25.02/06.03.202] 
(copy enclosed) is proper, legal and justified? If yes, to what relief the dependent of the deceased workman concerned 
is entitle to and what directions are necessary to the said management in this respect? ” 


(५ On receiving Order No. L-2202/08/2023-IR(CM-II) dated ३3].0.2023 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0I.02.2023 and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. Dhapru Das, son of Late Ch. Jagu Das filed written statement on 05.04.2023 through Koyala Mazdoor

Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL) and posted as an Underground Loader at Lachipur Colliery under Kajora 
Area. He died in harness on 26.05.2003, leaving behind his three sons namely, Budhan Das, Dhapru Das, K. Das, and

the date of death of his father, management of ECL held screening at the Colliery and Area level. He appeared before 
the Screening Committee on 27.08.2004 on the basis of letter dated 23.08.2004. After screening at the Area level, the 
dependent son was referred before the Initial Medical Examination Board for his medical examination in September, 
2004. Subsequently, the Manager of the Colliery informed the Dy. CPM, Kajora Area that one Latli Devi @ Tejni

3. Management contested the case and filed written statement on 0.05.2023. It is admitted that Ch. Jagu Das 
was a permanent employee of ECL and he died in harness on 26.05.2003. Dhapru Das, the son of the deceased

8. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, union representative, arguing for the dependent son of deceased employee submitted that 
the terms of NCWA is binding upon both the parties and as per Clause 9.3.l of NCWA one dependent of the deceased 
employee is entitled to employment, if the employee dies in harness. In the instant case Ch. Jagu Das died on 
26.05.2003 and within a very short period Dhapru Das, his elder son submitted a claim for employment on 
2.07.2003. The management processed his prayer for employment and held Screening and medical examination and 
thereafter the proposal was forwarded for approval by the Competent Authority. It is asserted that necessary 
documents had been submitted by the claimant along with “No Objection” from other legal heirs. It is argued that 
Jumni Devi, the wife of Ch. Jagu Das is the nominee in respect of the service benefits of Ch. Jagu Das and her name is 
recorded in the PS-4 Form, which is produced as Exhibit W-6. Jumni Devi died in the year 996 and till the death of 
Ch. Jagu Das did not contact a second marriage nor was the name of Tejni Devi recorded in the Service Record of the 
employee as the wife. It is argued that a criminal case filed by Tejni Devi at Giridih Court against the claimant and 
other family members of Ch. Jagu Das cannot be a ground for depriving Dhapru Das from his legitimate right of 
employment as a dependent. The union representative strenuously argued that the procedure was near to completion in 
the year 2004 but the management of ECL without any cogent reason stopped processing the prayer for 
employment on the basis of an unfounded complaint of Tejni Devi. Mr. Kumar further argued that the management of 
ECL has not been impleaded in any court case by Tejni Devi nor was the management restrained from processing the 
claim for employment of Dhapru Das. It is argued on behalf of the dependent son that delay has been caused at the 
instance of the officials of the management, resulting in immense hardship and suffering to the dependent son. Union 
reiterated the claimed for providing employment to the dependent son without further delay. 


9. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL, in reply argued that more than twenty years 
have lapsed since the death of the employee and this Industrial Dispute referred after twenty years is a stale one, 
without merit and the same is liable to be dismissed. 


0. Heard arguments advanced on behalf of the union and management, considered the pleadings and evidence 
adduced by both parties. The admitted position in this case was that Ch. Jagu Das is a permanent employee of ECL, 
who died in harness on 26.05.2003 leaving behind Dhapru Das along with two other sons and four daughters. It may 
be gathered from the evidence on record that Jumni Devi, the wife of the ex-employee predeceased her husband. It is 
also undisputed that Dhapru Das, the dependent son claimed employment under ECL by submitting her application on 
2.07.2003, which is within two months from the date of death of Ch. Jagu Das. The name of Dhapru Das has been 
recorded in the Service Record Excerpt of Ch. Jagu Das, which has been produced as Exhibit W-4 and in Form PS-3 
(Exhibit W-5), which is a record regarding particulars of the family of the employee. The age of Dhapru Das was 
recorded as 4 years as on 0I.04.987. Therefore, on 26.05.2003 he was 20 years of age and he was within the eligible 
age for employment as required in NCWA. On the basis of letter dated 23.08.2004 issued by the Personnel 
Manager, Kajora Area, an Office Order was passed on 26.08.2004 (Exhibit W-7) whereby Dhapru Das was advised 
to appear before the Screening Committee at Kajora Area Office on 27.08.2004 along with original documents like 
Death Certificate, Death Registration Certificate, Identity Card, S.P.E. Form, Indemnity Bond and School Certificate 
of the nominee, if any. Subsequently, on 5.09.2004 a letter was issued by the Manager, Lachipur Colliery, whereby 
Dhapru Das was requested to attend Kajora Area Medical Hospital for his medical examination, along with 
photographs and original documents. Copy of the said letter has been produced as Exhibit W-8. It appears from the 
record that appropriate proceedings were initiated by the management and no adverse findings was there in respect of 
the claim of Dhapru Das. According to the management the dispute cropped up when they received a complaint from 


590 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MARCH |4, 2026/PHALGUNA 23, 947 [PART II—SEc. 3(ii)] 


one Latli Devi @ Tejni Devi claiming herself to be the second wife of Ch. Jagu Das. The management issued a letter 
to the Dy. Chief Personnel Manager, Kajora Area dated 08.05.2006 informing that Tejni Devi has raised objection 
against providing employment to Dhapru Das in place of Ch. Jagu Das. According to the workman witness Tejni Devi 
is not the second wife of Ch. Jagu Das and her name has not been recorded as his wife even after the death of his 
mother. It appears from Exhibit W-6, which is a copy of Form PS-4, relating to nomination in respect of service 
benefits of Ch. Jagu Das that the name of Jumni Devi has been recorded as nominee and described as the wife with 
hundred percent (00%) share. Therefore, the management of ECL should not have entertained the complaint of Tejni 
Devi to stop the employment process as her claim had no legal foundation and the documents in the custody of the 
management of ECL could not have accommodated such extraneous claim. To set the dispute at rest Dhapru Das 
submitted a copy of judgement of acquittal passed by the learned District and Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 
I, Giridih in Criminal Appeal No. 46/20l0 (Exhibit W-) dated 3.03.204, setting aside an order passed by the 
Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Giridih on 20.05.200, where Dhapru Das had been held guilty under Section 
498(A) of the Indian Penal Code. The management of ECL by any competent court was never impleaded in any civil 
suit nor was there any order of restrainment against the management of ECL preventing it from providing employment 
to the son of deceased employee on the basis of the NCWA. The criminal case in which the petitioner son was 
entangled was finally disposed of in the year 204 but the management remained silent for seven long years to add to 
the delay and did not carry out its solemn responsibility of honouring the provisions of NCWA in its true perspective. 
The manner in which the prayer of Dhapru Das was delt with by different tiers of management of ECL only reveals 
their deliberate act of delaying the matter to frustrate and exhaust the claim for which the petitioner son is not 
responsible in any manner. It was only on 26.02.202l the Chief Manager, Kajora Area, issued a letter bearing No. 
ECL/CKC/P&IR/C-6/202/55 (Exhibit W-3) to Dhapru Das, informing that the employment proposal has been 
examined by the Competent Authority and observed as follows : 


“ The aforementioned employment proposal of Sri Dhapru das has been examined and it is found that the 
appointment of compassionate ground is given only to help a family to tide over the stringent financial crisis resulting 
from the sudden death of employee. 


Whereas, in this case, family members of the ex- employee indulged themselves in to their internal dispute 
which was ultimately dragged themselves in to court and a substantial period of about 768 years is now over. 
Therefore, essence of compassionate appointment is defeated in this case. 


Further, it is observed that, candidate is trying to procure employment as a matter of right. 


Whereas, Honorable Court had held that appointment on compassionate ground cannot be claimed as matter 
of right.” 


It needs to be born in mind that there is a presumption of innocence in favour of a person even when he is facing a 
criminal charge in a trial. It is only after he is convicted, an inference can be drawn against him. In the present case 
simply by lodging a complaint against Dhapru Das cannot stall the proceeding for his employment as per provisions 
of NCWA. The legal right of a dependent which has arisen out of the provision of NCWA cannot be curtailed on the 
basis of a complaint before the Criminal Court. In order to bank upon a contention that a family dispute prevailed with 
counter claims in respect of the service claimed by one of the dependents of deceased employee, the management 
should be in a position to establish that a Civil dispute had been initiated against the claimant as well as the 
management of the company, raising objection against such claim. In the present case management has relied upon a 
decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd Vs. Anil Badyakar and 
Others [Civil Appeal No. 3597 of 2009], wherein the Hon’ble Apex Court held : 


atic the compassionate appointment is not a vested right which can be exercised at any time in future. The 
compassionate employment cannot be claimed and offered after a lapse of time and after the crisis is over. In the 
instant case the employee died in harness in the year /967 and after a long squabble by the dependents of the 
deceased, they arrived at a settlement that the son-in-law of the second daughter who is unemployed may request for 
appointment on compassionate grounds. The request so made was accepted by the Personal Manager of the Company 
subject to the approval of the Director of the Company. The Director (P), who is the competent authority for post 
facto approval, keeping in view the object and purpose of providing compassionate appointment has cancelled the 
provisional appointment on the ground that nearly after 72 years from the date of death of the employee such an 
appointment could not have been offered to the so called dependent of the deceased employee. In our considered view, 
the decision of the employer was in consonance with Umesh Kumar Nagpal’s case and the same should not have been 
interfered with by the High Court.” 


ll. The facts of the present case is distinguishable from the facts of the case relied upon by the management of 
ECL. In the instant case Dhapru Das, the dependent son submitted his application claiming employment against the 
death of his father as per provisions of Clause 9.3.! of NCWA. Such claim was made within two months from the date 
of death of his father. There is no dispute that he is a dependent of the deceased employee and his name appeared as 
son in the Service Record Excerpt and the family particulars of the deceased employee for which such documents are 
maintained. The screening and medical examination of the candidate was also carried out within a reasonable period 
and documents were submitted. The stage was set for final consideration of the claim for employment when on the 


[भाग I—davs 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 4, 2026/फाल्गुन 23, 947 59] 


basis of a complaint submitted by Tejni Devi, management thought it wise not to proceed further in processing the 
claim for employment. Management representatives did not apply their mind that Tejni Devi did not figure in the 
Service Record of the deceased employee at any point of time. Therefore, management acted in a grossly illegal and 
arbitrary manner by entertaining the claim of Tejni Devi and thereby deprived the dependent son of the deceased 
employee from his rightful claim for employment for nearly 20 years. In the case of Anil Badyakar and Others 
(Supra.) there was a long dispute against the dependents of the deceased employee leading to delay in submitting 
claim for employment. The circumstances in this case is entirely different. Therefore, I hold that the ratio of the 
decision relied upon by the management does not apply to the facts and circumstances of this case. 


2. In the case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 
2024] the Hon’ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta held : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is a 
settlement under section 2 (p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, /947 and has binding effect on the parties thereto under 
section 76 (3) of the Act of /947. NCWA has made provisions for compassionate appointment for the dependents of 
the deceased employee.” The Hon'ble High Court further held that none of the clauses 9.3.0 to 9.5.0 of NCWA 
provide any time limit for applying or prescribe any financial solvency of the family as a disqualification. It does not 
allow the employer to choose between the dependents as to who it would grant the employment or the MMCC. The 
position of law is clearly settled that a claim for employment under NCWA is not treated as a compassionate 
appointment, depending upon the financial status of the family of the deceased employee. Nowhere, in the NCWA it 
has been stated that such employment was been provided only to the dependents to tide over sudden crisis resulting 
due to sudden death of the bread-earner or only in cases where the family of the deceased is in a penury. The terms of 
providing employment have gone beyond such consideration and has only specified the eligible age and physical 
fitness of the candidate to be considered for the employment. In order to turn down the claim for employment of a 
dependent on the ground that there has been lapse of time and the sudden crisis due to the death of the employee is 
over, the provisions of NCWA needs to be revised and necessary changes should be incorporated before regretting the 
prayer for employment on the ground of delay. From the factual matrix of this case, I find that the delay has been 
caused at the instance of the management by stalling the proceeding on the basis of frivolous complaint from a person 
who does not figure as a family member of the deceased in the Service Record. Since the delay in finalizing the claim 
for employment can be attributed to the management, the dependent son is not liable to suffer the loss. Therefore, I 
hold that the decision of the management communicated through their letter dated 26.02.202l / 06.03.202 are not 
legally tenable. This is an appropriate case where the management of ECL shall be directed to provide employment to 
Dhapru Das after completing the process of employment within two months from the date of communication of the 
Award. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Lachipur Colliery under Kajora 
Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to provide 
employment to Dhapru Das, the dependent son of Late Ch. Jagu Das, ex-employee of Eastern Coalfields Limited after 
completing the formalities related to employment within two months form the date of communication of the Award. 
Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry 
of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERIEE, Presiding Officer
